| Traffic Assistant | Level 4 | Rs 25,500 | about Rs 44,000 |
| Commercial cum Ticket Clerk | Level 3 | Rs 21,700 | about Rs 38,000 |
| Junior Clerk cum Typist | Level 2 | Rs 19,900 | about Rs 35,000 |

Take a Station Master as a worked example. On a basic of Rs 35,400, dearness allowance at 60 percent adds Rs 21,240, house rent allowance at the metro rate of 30 percent adds Rs 10,620, and transport allowance with DA adds roughly Rs 3,600. That is a gross near Rs 70,800, and after the National Pension System contribution and other deductions the in-hand lands close to Rs 62,000 a month. Railway staff also get pass facilities, medical cover, and other service benefits on top of pay, which lift the real value of the job well above the cash salary.

## Cut-off and normalization

Because RRB NTPC runs across many shifts and days, the boards apply normalization: your raw score is adjusted for the relative difficulty of your shift, so two candidates with identical raw marks in different shifts can end with different normalized scores. The merit list uses these normalized scores, not raw marks. This is why a candidate can clear the qualifying percentage yet miss the shortlist, and why comparing raw marks with a friend in another shift tells you little.

Official category-wise cut-offs are published per RRB region with the scorecards. For the Graduate cycle, the CBT 1 result on 11 June 2026 shortlisted about 88,037 candidates for CBT 2 against 5,810 posts, an effective ratio close to 15 to 1 at that stage. Cut-offs vary by region, category, and the vacancy pool of each RRB, so read the figure for your own board rather than an all-India number.

## What each post actually does

The post you land shapes your working life far more than the pay level alone. A Station Master runs train operations at a station, controls signals and platform movement, and works rotating shifts through the night, which is why the role carries the CBAT aptitude screen. A Goods Train Manager, the role that used to be called Goods Guard, travels with freight trains and is responsible for the safe running of the rake, a field job with frequent time away from home. The clerk cadres, from Senior Clerk to Junior Account Assistant, handle accounts, records, and commercial work in railway offices, which suits candidates who prefer fixed hours and a desk. Commercial cum Ticket Clerk and Trains Clerk roles deal with ticketing, parcel, and train documentation at stations. Reading the duty profile before you rank your post preference saves a lot of regret later, since a strong CBT 2 score in a role you dislike is a poor trade.

## Career growth in Indian Railways

RRB NTPC is an entry into a service with a clear promotion ladder rather than a dead-end clerical job. A Station Master can rise through Section Controller and into operating supervisor grades over a career. Clerk cadres move up from Senior Clerk to Head Clerk and into office superintendent roles, with departmental exams opening faster routes for those who prepare for them. Railway staff also receive pass and privilege-ticket facilities for themselves and their families, medical cover through railway hospitals, and pension benefits under the applicable scheme. These service benefits, taken together with the in-hand pay, are a large part of why railway jobs draw crores of applicants each cycle.

## Preparation strategy for RRB NTPC

The two-stage structure rewards a two-speed plan. CBT 1 is a speed test of basics, so the first phase of preparation should build accuracy and pace across all three sections, since a weak section drags the whole normalized score down. General Awareness carries the most questions in both stages, and it is the section where a daily current affairs habit and a static general knowledge revision pay off directly. Mathematics and reasoning reward pattern recognition, which comes from solving previous years' papers rather than reading theory. Once CBT 1 is behind you, shift to CBT 2 depth, where the higher question count and the same negative marking mean that managing which questions to skip becomes a skill in itself. Candidates aiming for Station Master or Traffic Assistant should also practise the CBAT format early, because the aptitude batteries test traits that improve with familiarity and cannot be crammed the night before.

## Exam day and documents

Carry a printed admit card and the same photo ID you used at registration, since the biometric check at the centre matches both. Reach early, because railway exam centres run tight entry cut-off times and latecomers are not admitted. The test is computer based, so a rough sheet is provided and must be returned before you leave. Do not carry electronic devices, smart watches, or written material, as these lead to disqualification. Check your regional RRB website the night before for any last-minute centre or timing notice.

## How to apply and track your status

Applications for both 2026 cycles have closed, so the current task is tracking the exam and result stages. Log in at the RRB application portal (rrbapply.gov.in) with your registration number to download admit cards and scorecards, and watch your regional RRB website for cut-off and result notices. Admit cards release about four days before each exam, with a city intimation slip a few days earlier. Keep your registration number and password safe, since every stage from CBT 2 result to document verification is handled through the same login.

## Frequently asked questions

**How many vacancies are there in RRB NTPC 2026?**
RRB NTPC 2026 has 8,868 vacancies in total, split into 5,810 posts at the Graduate level (CEN 06/2025) and 3,058 posts at the Undergraduate level (CEN 07/2025), across all Railway Recruitment Board regions.

**What is the RRB NTPC 2026 CBT 2 exam date?**
The Graduate level CBT 2 was held on 10 July 2026, and its answer key was released on 15 July 2026. The Undergraduate level CBT 2 was scheduled for 17 September 2026, per the RRB exam notice.

**Which RRB NTPC posts require the CBAT?**
Only Station Master and Traffic Assistant require the Computer Based Aptitude Test. For these two posts the final merit is 70 percent CBT 2 and 30 percent CBAT, and a candidate must score at least a 42 T-score in every test battery with no category relaxation.

**What is the in-hand salary of a Station Master in RRB NTPC?**
A Station Master at Pay Level 6 with a basic of Rs 35,400 takes home about Rs 62,000 a month in a metro, at the 60 percent dearness allowance effective 1 January 2026, after HRA, transport allowance, and deductions.

**What is the age limit for RRB NTPC 2026?**
The age limit, reckoned as on 1 January 2026, is 18 to 33 years for the Graduate level and 18 to 30 years for the Undergraduate level, before relaxation of 3 years for OBC, 5 years for SC and ST, and up to 15 years for PwBD.

**Is there negative marking in RRB NTPC?**
Yes. Both CBT 1 and CBT 2 carry a penalty of one-third of a mark for every wrong answer. The CBAT for Station Master and Traffic Assistant has no negative marking.

**What is the difference between the Graduate and Undergraduate levels?**
The Graduate level (CEN 06/2025) needs a bachelor's degree and fills higher-paid posts like Station Master and Goods Train Manager at Levels 4 to 6. The Undergraduate level (CEN 07/2025) needs a Class 12 pass and fills clerk posts at Levels 2 to 3.

**Are RRB NTPC 2026 applications still open?**
No. Applications for both the Graduate and Undergraduate cycles closed in November 2025. The recruitment is now in its exam, answer key, and result stages, which the Railway Recruitment Boards announce region by region.

**Do CBT 1 marks count in the final merit?**
No. CBT 1 is a screening test used only to shortlist candidates for CBT 2 at about 20 times the vacancies. The final merit rests on CBT 2, plus the CBAT for Station Master and Traffic Assistant posts.

## NDA & NA 2026 at a glance

The UPSC National Defence Academy and Naval Academy Examination, NDA & NA, is the main route into the armed forces straight after Class 12, leading to a commission as an officer in the Army, Navy, or Air Force. UPSC conducts it twice a year, as NDA I and NDA II. NDA II 2026 is now past its written stage. UPSC notified it on 20 May 2026 for 394 vacancies and held the written exam on 13 September 2026, with Mathematics from 10:00 am to 12:30 pm and the General Ability Test from 2:00 pm to 4:30 pm. NDA I 2026 is a completed cycle.

Two things make this exam stand out. It is one of the few officer entries open right after Class 12, at an age of 16.5 to 19.5, and, since a Supreme Court ruling, it is open to women across all wings. This guide covers the two cycles, the women-eligibility position clearly, the written exam and the five-day SSB interview, and the honest difference between the stipend during training and the pay after commissioning.

What candidates are waiting for now is the written result. The NDA I 2026 cycle sets the expectation: its written exam was on 12 April 2026 and UPSC put out the roll-number result on 8 May 2026, twenty-six days later, followed by the name-wise list on 13 May 2026. On that pace the NDA II written result falls in the first half of October 2026, though UPSC publishes no advance date. Qualified candidates then register on the Indian Army recruitment portal within two weeks of the result to be allotted an SSB centre and dates. NDA I 2027 is the next fresh cycle.

## Important dates for NDA & NA 2026

| Event | NDA II 2026 (live) | NDA I 2026 (baseline) |
|---|---|---|
| Notification | 20 May 2026 | 10 December 2025 |
| Written exam | 13 September 2026 | 12 April 2026 |
| Written result | Awaited | 8 May 2026 (13 May by name) |
| SSB registration | Within 2 weeks of result | Within 2 weeks of result |
| Course | NDA 158th and 120th Naval Academy Course | NDA 157th and 119th Naval Academy Course |

## Vacancy details

NDA II 2026 has 394 vacancies, of which 370 are for male candidates and 24 for female candidates. The commonly reported service-wise split is Army 208, Air Force 120, Navy 42, and Naval Academy 24, though the exact split is set in the notification, so confirm it there. The Naval Academy figure is the 10+2 Cadet Entry Scheme intake.

## Women in the NDA

This is a point competitors often state flatly or bury, so it is worth explaining clearly. Following a Supreme Court order in 2021, unmarried women became eligible for the NDA, and the first women cadets were admitted from the 2022 intake. Women are now eligible across all wings, that is the Army, Navy, Air Force, and Naval Academy, subject to the same age, education, and medical standards, with the physical standards set to female norms. In NDA II 2026, 24 of the 394 seats are earmarked for women. So a woman candidate who has passed or is appearing in Class 12, meets the age band, and satisfies the wing-specific subject requirement can sit the NDA exactly as a male candidate does.

## Eligibility for NDA & NA 2026

On age, you must be between 16.5 and 19.5 years, and unmarried. The exact birth-date window is set for each cycle in the notification, and there is no age relaxation for any category.

On education, you need to have passed or be appearing in Class 12. The subject requirement depends on the wing. For the Army wing, any stream is accepted, so Arts and Commerce candidates qualify. For the Navy, Air Force, and Naval Academy wings, Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics, that is the PCM combination, is mandatory. This distinction matters and many pages leave it vague: a candidate without PCM can still join the Army wing but not the Navy or Air Force.

On marital status, you must be unmarried, and you must remain unmarried until you complete training.

## Physical and medical standards

Candidates must meet the physical and medical standards for a cadet, which are set out in the notification. The minimum height is around 157 cm for the Army and Navy and higher for the Air Force, with relaxations for candidates from Gorkha, North-Eastern, Garhwal, and Kumaon regions. Vision standards are stricter for the Air Force, where spectacles are not permitted for the flying branch, and procedures like LASIK or radial keratotomy are disqualifying. Candidates should read the medical standards carefully before applying, since a medical disqualification later is a hard setback.

## Selection process

NDA selection has two stages that together carry 1800 marks.

1. Written examination: 900 marks. This shortlists candidates for the SSB.
2. Services Selection Board (SSB) interview: 900 marks, a five-day assessment.

The final merit is built from the written exam and the SSB together, so both carry equal weight, and a candidate must clear the SSB, not just the written exam, to be selected.

## Written exam pattern

The written exam has two papers on the same day, both objective and bilingual, with different negative marking.

| Paper | Content | Questions | Marks | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Paper 1 | Mathematics | 120 | 300 | 2.5 hours |
| Paper 2 | General Ability Test (GAT) | 150 | 600 | 2.5 hours |

The General Ability Test is split into English for 200 marks and General Knowledge for 400 marks. Each question carries 2.5 marks. The negative marking differs by paper: Mathematics deducts about 0.83 marks per wrong answer, and the General Ability Test deducts about 1.33 marks per wrong answer. So a wrong guess in the GAT is costlier than in Maths, which shapes attempt strategy.

## Syllabus

Mathematics covers algebra, matrices and determinants, trigonometry, analytical geometry in two and three dimensions, differential and integral calculus, differential equations, vector algebra, and statistics and probability, with trigonometry, algebra, and calculus forming the bulk. The General Ability Test covers English grammar, vocabulary, and comprehension, and General Knowledge across Physics, Chemistry, General Science, History, Geography, and current affairs. The standard is broadly that of Class 11 and 12, drawing largely on the NCERT textbooks.

## The five-day SSB interview

The SSB interview is where many written-qualified candidates fall, because it tests officer-like qualities rather than knowledge, and it runs over five days.

Day one is screening, with an officer intelligence rating test and a picture perception and discussion test, after which some candidates are sent home. Day two is the psychology round, with a thematic apperception test, a word association test, a situation reaction test, and a self-description. Days three and four are the group testing officer tasks, including group discussions, group planning, progressive group tasks, and command tasks, alongside the personal interview. Day five is the conference, where the board takes its final call. The SSB assesses qualities like reasoning, decision-making, initiative, and the ability to work in and lead a group, so preparation for it is different from exam study and rewards mock SSBs and self-awareness.

## What the NDA cutoff has actually been

UPSC publishes the cutoff marks after each cycle closes, and the numbers move a lot from year to year, which is why a single "expected cutoff" figure from a coaching site is worth very little. These are the official UPSC cutoffs for recent NDA I cycles.

| Cycle | Written cutoff (out of 900) | Final cutoff (out of 1800) |
|---|---|---|
| NDA I 2025 | 334 | 699 |
| NDA I 2024 | 291 | 654 |
| NDA I 2023 | 301 | 664 |
| NDA I 2022 | 360 | 720 |
| NDA I 2021 | 343 | 709 |
| NDA I 2020 | 355 | 723 |

Two things stand out from that table. The written cutoff has swung between 291 and 360 marks in six cycles, a spread of 69 marks, which tracks paper difficulty rather than any trend you can plan around. And the gap between the written cutoff and the final cutoff sits at roughly 360 to 370 marks in every year, which tells you what the SSB adds: a candidate who scrapes through the written exam still needs a solid SSB performance to make the final list.

Alongside the aggregate cutoff, UPSC applies a minimum qualifying standard of 25 per cent in each subject. A candidate who clears the aggregate but falls below 25 per cent in Mathematics or in the General Ability Test is not evaluated further, so lopsided preparation that abandons one paper does not work here.

A practical target: aim for 400 or more in the written exam rather than the 300 to 350 band. That builds a cushion against a hard paper and against an average SSB day.

## Stipend during training versus pay after commissioning

This is where honesty matters, because other pages blur a cadet's training stipend with an officer's salary. During the roughly three years at the NDA and the further year at the service academy, cadets do not draw a full officer salary; their food, accommodation, uniforms, and medical care are provided, and a stipend applies in the final pre-commission training year, commonly cited at around Rs 56,100 a month. That figure is the pre-commission stipend, not a multi-year salary.

On being commissioned as a Lieutenant or the equivalent, an officer enters Pay Level 10 with a basic pay of Rs 56,100, plus Military Service Pay of Rs 15,500 and dearness allowance, which brings the in-hand to roughly Rs 1,00,000 to Rs 1,25,000 a month, alongside subsidised housing, rations, and other service benefits. The pay then grows through the officer ranks over a career. So the accurate picture is a modest stipend during training and a strong officer package after commissioning, not a large salary from day one.

## What happens after selection: the training path

Selection into the NDA starts a four-year training path, not a posting. Cadets from all three services train together for three years at the National Defence Academy at Khadakwasla near Pune, then move to their service academy for about a year of specialised training.

| Wing | Service academy after NDA | Location |
|---|---|---|
| Army | Indian Military Academy (IMA) | Dehradun |
| Navy | Indian Naval Academy (INA) | Ezhimala |
| Air Force | Air Force Academy (AFA) | Dundigal, Hyderabad |

During the three years at Khadakwasla, cadets also read for a bachelor's degree affiliated to Jawaharlal Nehru University, in one of BA, BSc, or BSc Computer Science, and the degree is awarded at the passing out parade. So a cadet who completes NDA training leaves with a recognised graduate degree as well as a military commission, which matters if a career ever moves outside the services.

Candidates who take the Naval Academy route through the 10+2 Cadet Entry Scheme go directly to INA Ezhimala rather than through Khadakwasla, and read for a BTech there.

The commission comes at the end of the service academy year, not at the end of the NDA years. That is the point at which the stipend becomes an officer's pay.

## Career progression after commissioning

An officer commissioned through the NDA enters as a Lieutenant in the Army, or a Sub Lieutenant in the Navy and a Flying Officer in the Air Force, and moves up through defined pay levels under the 7th Pay Commission. Military Service Pay of Rs 15,500 a month applies at every one of these ranks, on top of basic pay and dearness allowance.

| Army rank | Navy equivalent | Air Force equivalent | Pay level |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lieutenant | Sub Lieutenant | Flying Officer | Level 10 |
| Captain | Lieutenant | Flight Lieutenant | Level 10B |
| Major | Lieutenant Commander | Squadron Leader | Level 11 |
| Lieutenant Colonel | Commander | Wing Commander | Level 12A |
| Colonel | Captain | Group Captain | Level 13 |
| Brigadier | Commodore | Air Commodore | Level 13A |
| Major General | Rear Admiral | Air Vice Marshal | Level 14 |

Promotion to Captain and Major is time-bound, at roughly two and six years of service, so an NDA entrant reaches Major in their late twenties. Above Lieutenant Colonel, promotion turns selective and depends on vacancies, annual reports, and courses. Beyond pay, the package includes subsidised accommodation, ration entitlements, medical cover for the officer and dependants under ECHS after retirement, group insurance, and a pension, which is the part of the deal that separates a permanent commission from the four-year Agniveer route covered on our [Indian Army Agniveer](/sarkari-naukri/indian-army-agniveer-2026) page.

## NDA versus CDS versus CAPF

Candidates aiming at an officer career often weigh NDA against the [UPSC CDS](/sarkari-naukri/upsc-cds-ii-2026) route after graduation and the [CAPF Assistant Commandant](/sarkari-naukri/upsc-capf-ac-2026) route into the paramilitary. This comparison sets out the difference.

| Factor | NDA | CDS | CAPF AC |
|---|---|---|---|
| Entry after | Class 12 | Graduation | Graduation |
| Age | 16.5 to 19.5 | About 19 to 25 | 20 to 25 |
| Force | Army, Navy, Air Force | Army, Navy, Air Force | Central armed police forces |
| Women eligible | Yes, all wings | Yes, via specified entries | Yes |
| Selection | Written plus SSB | Written plus SSB | Written plus physical plus interview |

NDA is the earliest officer entry, straight after Class 12. CDS is the graduate route into the armed forces. CAPF AC leads into the paramilitary forces. A candidate who is still in Class 12 and set on the armed forces should target NDA, while graduates would look at CDS or CAPF AC.

## A preparation plan for NDA

NDA rewards a steady build across Maths and the General Ability Test alongside SSB readiness. For Maths, revise the Class 11 and 12 syllabus thoroughly, since trigonometry, algebra, and calculus dominate, and practise under the negative-marking scheme. For the GAT, build English through reading and grammar practice, and General Knowledge through NCERT science and social science plus a daily current-affairs habit, keeping in mind the heavier negative marking that punishes loose guessing. Just as important, prepare for the SSB in parallel, since it carries half the marks and cannot be crammed; mock interviews, group tasks, and honest self-reflection build the officer-like qualities the board looks for. The candidates who convert NDA are those who treated the SSB as seriously as the written exam.

## Books and resources for NDA preparation

The syllabus sits at Class 11 and 12 level, so the NCERT textbooks do most of the work and specialised NDA books fill the gaps in practice and pattern.

| Section | What to use |
|---|---|
| Mathematics | NCERT Class 11 and 12 Maths, then Pathfinder for NDA and NA (Arihant) or R S Aggarwal for practice |
| English | Objective General English by S P Bakshi, plus daily newspaper reading for comprehension |
| General Knowledge | NCERT Science and Social Science for Classes 9 to 12, Lucent's General Knowledge for revision |
| Current affairs | A monthly current affairs compilation, or a daily newspaper habit over 6 to 8 months |
| Previous papers | UPSC NDA question papers of the last 8 to 10 cycles, available free on upsc.gov.in |
| SSB | Let Us Crack SSB Interview, plus mock SSB sessions if you can access them |

Previous years' papers do more than any single book. UPSC repeats question types heavily in the General Ability Test, and working through 8 to 10 past papers under timed conditions teaches the negative-marking calculus better than reading about it.

## Mistakes that cost NDA candidates

A few errors show up cycle after cycle, and every one of them is avoidable.

1. Applying for the wrong wing. A candidate without Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics who marks Navy or Air Force preferences is rejected at document verification, after months of preparation.
2. Ignoring the medical standards until the end. Vision requirements for the flying branch disqualify a large number of otherwise strong candidates, and refractive surgery like LASIK is disqualifying for the Air Force. Read the medical standards before you apply, not after you clear the written exam.
3. Guessing freely in the General Ability Test. At about 1.33 marks deducted per wrong answer against 2.5 for a correct one, loose guessing across 30 uncertain questions can cost more than it gains.
4. Treating the SSB as an afterthought. It carries 900 of the 1800 marks, and the gap between the written and final cutoffs shows exactly how much it decides.
5. Missing the age window. The 16.5 to 19.5 band is narrow and has no relaxation for any category, so a candidate typically gets only two or three attempts in total.
6. Letting one paper slide. The 25 per cent per-subject minimum means a strong Maths score cannot rescue a weak General Ability Test.

## How to apply for NDA

Applications go through the UPSC online portal, and the process is the same in every cycle.

1. Complete the One Time Registration on upsconline.nic.in if you have not already. This is a separate step from the application itself and is reused across UPSC exams.
2. Open the NDA and NA application when the notification goes live and fill in personal, educational, and communication details exactly as they appear on your Class 10 certificate.
3. Choose your wing preferences in order, keeping the PCM requirement in mind for Navy, Air Force, and Naval Academy.
4. Pick your exam centre. Centres fill on a first-apply basis, so applying early gives you a better chance of a nearby centre.
5. Upload your photograph and signature in the specified format, along with a photo ID.
6. Pay the fee of Rs 100. Women candidates and SC and ST candidates pay nothing.
7. Submit, then save the PDF and the registration number. UPSC opens a short correction window after the deadline for limited edits.

## Documents you will need

Keep these ready for the application and the SSB.

1. Your Class 10 and Class 12 certificates and mark sheets, with the wing-specific subjects.
2. Proof of date of birth, usually your Class 10 certificate.
3. A recent photograph, signature, and a valid photo ID matching your application.
4. Documents for any regional height relaxation and other certificates as listed in the notification.

## Frequently asked questions

**Can girls apply for NDA in 2026?**
Yes. Following a Supreme Court order in 2021, unmarried women are eligible for the NDA across all wings, that is the Army, Navy, Air Force, and Naval Academy, with the first women cadets admitted from the 2022 intake. In NDA II 2026, 24 of the 394 seats are earmarked for women.

**What is the NDA 2026 exam date?**
The NDA II 2026 written exam was held on 13 September 2026, and the earlier NDA I 2026 written exam on 12 April 2026. UPSC conducts the NDA and NA examination twice a year, as NDA I and NDA II.


**When will the NDA 2 2026 written result be declared?**
UPSC has not announced a date. The closest guide is the NDA I 2026 cycle, where the written exam was on 12 April 2026 and the roll-number result appeared on 8 May 2026, with the name-wise list on 13 May 2026. Applying that twenty-six day gap to the 13 September 2026 exam puts the NDA II result in the first half of October 2026. Results are published on upsc.gov.in and nowhere else first.

**Has UPSC released the official NDA 2 2026 answer key?**
No, and it will not for some time. UPSC publishes official answer keys in the Answer Keys section of upsc.gov.in only after a cycle's entire selection process is finished, which for NDA means after the SSB stage and the final result. The set-wise keys circulating within days of the exam come from coaching institutes, not from UPSC, and they differ from each other on the harder General Ability questions. Treat a score calculated from one as an estimate with a margin of several marks, not as a number to plan around.

**What happens between the NDA written result and the SSB interview?**
Candidates who clear the written stage register on the Indian Army recruitment portal within two weeks of the result, and the Services Selection Board then allots a centre and dates. The SSB runs five days and carries 900 marks, the same weight as the written paper, so the final merit out of 1,800 is decided as much at the board as in the exam hall. NDA I 2026 SSB interviews ran from June to September 2026, which is the spread to plan around.

**Is PCM compulsory for NDA?**
It depends on the wing. Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics are mandatory for the Navy, Air Force, and Naval Academy wings. The Army wing accepts any stream, so an Arts or Commerce candidate can join the Army wing without PCM but not the Navy or Air Force.

**What is the age limit for NDA 2026?**
Candidates must be between 16.5 and 19.5 years and unmarried, with the exact birth-date window set for each cycle in the notification. There is no age relaxation for any category.

**Do NDA cadets get a salary during training?**
Not a full salary. Cadets get free food, accommodation, uniforms, and medical care during training, and a stipend of around Rs 56,100 a month applies in the final pre-commission training year. A full officer package, with basic pay, Military Service Pay, and allowances, begins only on commissioning.

**What is the total marks of the NDA exam?**
The NDA selection carries 1800 marks in total: the written exam is 900 marks (Mathematics 300 plus General Ability Test 600), and the SSB interview is 900 marks. The final merit is built from both together.

**Is there negative marking in NDA?**
Yes. The Mathematics paper deducts about 0.83 marks for each wrong answer, and the General Ability Test deducts about 1.33 marks per wrong answer. Because the GAT penalty is heavier, blind guessing there is costlier than in Maths.

**Can I join NDA after 12th with Arts or Commerce?**
Yes, but only the Army wing. The Army wing accepts any stream, so Arts and Commerce candidates qualify. The Navy, Air Force, and Naval Academy wings require Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics.

**What is the difference between NDA and CDS?**
NDA is the officer entry straight after Class 12, at 16.5 to 19.5 years, while CDS is the graduate route into the armed forces at about 19 to 25 years. Both use a written exam plus the SSB interview, but NDA is the earlier entry and CDS is for graduates.

## Important dates for NDA & NA 2026

| Event | NDA II 2026 (live) | NDA I 2026 (baseline) |
|---|---|---|
| Notification | 20 May 2026 | 10 December 2025 |
| Written exam | 13 September 2026 | 12 April 2026 |
| Course | NDA 158th and 120th Naval Academy Course | NDA 157th and 119th Naval Academy Course |

This is a point competitors often state flatly or bury, so it is worth explaining clearly. Following a Supreme Court order in 2021, unmarried women became eligible for the NDA, and the first women cadets were admitted from the 2022 intake. Women are now eligible across all wings, that is the Army, Navy, Air Force, and Naval Academy, subject to the same age, education, and medical standards, with the physical standards set to female norms. In NDA II 2026, 24 of the 394 seats are earmarked for women. So a woman candidate who has passed or is appearing in Class 12, meets the age band, and satisfies the wing-specific subject requirement can sit the NDA exactly as a male candidate does.

## Eligibility for NDA & NA 2026

On age, you must be between 16.5 and 19.5 years, and unmarried. The exact birth-date window is set for each cycle in the notification, and there is no age relaxation for any category.

On education, you need to have passed or be appearing in Class 12. The subject requirement depends on the wing. For the Army wing, any stream is accepted, so Arts and Commerce candidates qualify. For the Navy, Air Force, and Naval Academy wings, Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics, that is the PCM combination, is mandatory. This distinction matters and many pages leave it vague: a candidate without PCM can still join the Army wing but not the Navy or Air Force.

On marital status, you must be unmarried, and you must remain unmarried until you complete training.

## Physical and medical standards

Candidates must meet the physical and medical standards for a cadet, which are set out in the notification. The minimum height is around 157 cm for the Army and Navy and higher for the Air Force, with relaxations for candidates from Gorkha, North-Eastern, Garhwal, and Kumaon regions. Vision standards are stricter for the Air Force, where spectacles are not permitted for the flying branch, and procedures like LASIK or radial keratotomy are disqualifying. Candidates should read the medical standards carefully before applying, since a medical disqualification later is a hard setback.

## Selection process

NDA selection has two stages that together carry 1800 marks.

1. Written examination: 900 marks. This shortlists candidates for the SSB.
2. Services Selection Board (SSB) interview: 900 marks, a five-day assessment.

The final merit is built from the written exam and the SSB together, so both carry equal weight, and a candidate must clear the SSB, not just the written exam, to be selected.

## Written exam pattern

The written exam has two papers on the same day, both objective and bilingual, with different negative marking.

| Paper | Content | Questions | Marks | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Paper 1 | Mathematics | 120 | 300 | 2.5 hours |
| Paper 2 | General Ability Test (GAT) | 150 | 600 | 2.5 hours |

The General Ability Test is split into English for 200 marks and General Knowledge for 400 marks. Each question carries 2.5 marks. The negative marking differs by paper: Mathematics deducts about 0.83 marks per wrong answer, and the General Ability Test deducts about 1.33 marks per wrong answer. So a wrong guess in the GAT is costlier than in Maths, which shapes attempt strategy.

## Syllabus

Mathematics covers algebra, matrices and determinants, trigonometry, analytical geometry in two and three dimensions, differential and integral calculus, differential equations, vector algebra, and statistics and probability, with trigonometry, algebra, and calculus forming the bulk. The General Ability Test covers English grammar, vocabulary, and comprehension, and General Knowledge across Physics, Chemistry, General Science, History, Geography, and current affairs. The standard is broadly that of Class 11 and 12, drawing largely on the NCERT textbooks.

## The five-day SSB interview

The SSB interview is where many written-qualified candidates fall, because it tests officer-like qualities rather than knowledge, and it runs over five days.

Day one is screening, with an officer intelligence rating test and a picture perception and discussion test, after which some candidates are sent home. Day two is the psychology round, with a thematic apperception test, a word association test, a situation reaction test, and a self-description. Days three and four are the group testing officer tasks, including group discussions, group planning, progressive group tasks, and command tasks, alongside the personal interview. Day five is the conference, where the board takes its final call. The SSB assesses qualities like reasoning, decision-making, initiative, and the ability to work in and lead a group, so preparation for it is different from exam study and rewards mock SSBs and self-awareness.

## What the NDA cutoff has actually been

UPSC publishes the cutoff marks after each cycle closes, and the numbers move a lot from year to year, which is why a single "expected cutoff" figure from a coaching site is worth very little. These are the official UPSC cutoffs for recent NDA I cycles.

| Cycle | Written cutoff (out of 900) | Final cutoff (out of 1800) |
|---|---|---|
| NDA I 2025 | 334 | 699 |
| NDA I 2024 | 291 | 654 |
| NDA I 2023 | 301 | 664 |
| NDA I 2022 | 360 | 720 |
| NDA I 2021 | 343 | 709 |
| NDA I 2020 | 355 | 723 |

Two things stand out from that table. The written cutoff has swung between 291 and 360 marks in six cycles, a spread of 69 marks, which tracks paper difficulty rather than any trend you can plan around. And the gap between the written cutoff and the final cutoff sits at roughly 360 to 370 marks in every year, which tells you what the SSB adds: a candidate who scrapes through the written exam still needs a solid SSB performance to make the final list.

Alongside the aggregate cutoff, UPSC applies a minimum qualifying standard of 25 per cent in each subject. A candidate who clears the aggregate but falls below 25 per cent in Mathematics or in the General Ability Test is not evaluated further, so lopsided preparation that abandons one paper does not work here.

A practical target: aim for 400 or more in the written exam rather than the 300 to 350 band. That builds a cushion against a hard paper and against an average SSB day.

## Stipend during training versus pay after commissioning

This is where honesty matters, because other pages blur a cadet's training stipend with an officer's salary. During the roughly three years at the NDA and the further year at the service academy, cadets do not draw a full officer salary; their food, accommodation, uniforms, and medical care are provided, and a stipend applies in the final pre-commission training year, commonly cited at around Rs 56,100 a month. That figure is the pre-commission stipend, not a multi-year salary.

On being commissioned as a Lieutenant or the equivalent, an officer enters Pay Level 10 with a basic pay of Rs 56,100, plus Military Service Pay of Rs 15,500 and dearness allowance, which brings the in-hand to roughly Rs 1,00,000 to Rs 1,25,000 a month, alongside subsidised housing, rations, and other service benefits. The pay then grows through the officer ranks over a career. So the accurate picture is a modest stipend during training and a strong officer package after commissioning, not a large salary from day one.

## What happens after selection: the training path

Selection into the NDA starts a four-year training path, not a posting. Cadets from all three services train together for three years at the National Defence Academy at Khadakwasla near Pune, then move to their service academy for about a year of specialised training.

| Wing | Service academy after NDA | Location |
|---|---|---|
| Army | Indian Military Academy (IMA) | Dehradun |
| Navy | Indian Naval Academy (INA) | Ezhimala |
| Air Force | Air Force Academy (AFA) | Dundigal, Hyderabad |

During the three years at Khadakwasla, cadets also read for a bachelor's degree affiliated to Jawaharlal Nehru University, in one of BA, BSc, or BSc Computer Science, and the degree is awarded at the passing out parade. So a cadet who completes NDA training leaves with a recognised graduate degree as well as a military commission, which matters if a career ever moves outside the services.

Candidates who take the Naval Academy route through the 10+2 Cadet Entry Scheme go directly to INA Ezhimala rather than through Khadakwasla, and read for a BTech there.

The commission comes at the end of the service academy year, not at the end of the NDA years. That is the point at which the stipend becomes an officer's pay.

## Career progression after commissioning

An officer commissioned through the NDA enters as a Lieutenant in the Army, or a Sub Lieutenant in the Navy and a Flying Officer in the Air Force, and moves up through defined pay levels under the 7th Pay Commission. Military Service Pay of Rs 15,500 a month applies at every one of these ranks, on top of basic pay and dearness allowance.

| Army rank | Navy equivalent | Air Force equivalent | Pay level |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lieutenant | Sub Lieutenant | Flying Officer | Level 10 |
| Captain | Lieutenant | Flight Lieutenant | Level 10B |
| Major | Lieutenant Commander | Squadron Leader | Level 11 |
| Lieutenant Colonel | Commander | Wing Commander | Level 12A |
| Colonel | Captain | Group Captain | Level 13 |
| Brigadier | Commodore | Air Commodore | Level 13A |
| Major General | Rear Admiral | Air Vice Marshal | Level 14 |

Promotion to Captain and Major is time-bound, at roughly two and six years of service, so an NDA entrant reaches Major in their late twenties. Above Lieutenant Colonel, promotion turns selective and depends on vacancies, annual reports, and courses. Beyond pay, the package includes subsidised accommodation, ration entitlements, medical cover for the officer and dependants under ECHS after retirement, group insurance, and a pension, which is the part of the deal that separates a permanent commission from the four-year Agniveer route covered on our [Indian Army Agniveer](/sarkari-naukri/indian-army-agniveer-2026) page.

## NDA versus CDS versus CAPF

Candidates aiming at an officer career often weigh NDA against the [UPSC CDS](/sarkari-naukri/upsc-cds-ii-2026) route after graduation and the [CAPF Assistant Commandant](/sarkari-naukri/upsc-capf-ac-2026) route into the paramilitary. This comparison sets out the difference.

| Factor | NDA | CDS | CAPF AC |
|---|---|---|---|
| Entry after | Class 12 | Graduation | Graduation |
| Age | 16.5 to 19.5 | About 19 to 25 | 20 to 25 |
| Force | Army, Navy, Air Force | Army, Navy, Air Force | Central armed police forces |
| Women eligible | Yes, all wings | Yes, via specified entries | Yes |
| Selection | Written plus SSB | Written plus SSB | Written plus physical plus interview |

NDA is the earliest officer entry, straight after Class 12. CDS is the graduate route into the armed forces. CAPF AC leads into the paramilitary forces. A candidate who is still in Class 12 and set on the armed forces should target NDA, while graduates would look at CDS or CAPF AC.

## A preparation plan for NDA

NDA rewards a steady build across Maths and the General Ability Test alongside SSB readiness. For Maths, revise the Class 11 and 12 syllabus thoroughly, since trigonometry, algebra, and calculus dominate, and practise under the negative-marking scheme. For the GAT, build English through reading and grammar practice, and General Knowledge through NCERT science and social science plus a daily current-affairs habit, keeping in mind the heavier negative marking that punishes loose guessing. Just as important, prepare for the SSB in parallel, since it carries half the marks and cannot be crammed; mock interviews, group tasks, and honest self-reflection build the officer-like qualities the board looks for. The candidates who convert NDA are those who treated the SSB as seriously as the written exam.

## Books and resources for NDA preparation

The syllabus sits at Class 11 and 12 level, so the NCERT textbooks do most of the work and specialised NDA books fill the gaps in practice and pattern.

| Section | What to use |
|---|---|
| Mathematics | NCERT Class 11 and 12 Maths, then Pathfinder for NDA and NA (Arihant) or R S Aggarwal for practice |
| English | Objective General English by S P Bakshi, plus daily newspaper reading for comprehension |
| General Knowledge | NCERT Science and Social Science for Classes 9 to 12, Lucent's General Knowledge for revision |
| Current affairs | A monthly current affairs compilation, or a daily newspaper habit over 6 to 8 months |
| Previous papers | UPSC NDA question papers of the last 8 to 10 cycles, available free on upsc.gov.in |
| SSB | Let Us Crack SSB Interview, plus mock SSB sessions if you can access them |

Previous years' papers do more than any single book. UPSC repeats question types heavily in the General Ability Test, and working through 8 to 10 past papers under timed conditions teaches the negative-marking calculus better than reading about it.

## Mistakes that cost NDA candidates

A few errors show up cycle after cycle, and every one of them is avoidable.

1. Applying for the wrong wing. A candidate without Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics who marks Navy or Air Force preferences is rejected at document verification, after months of preparation.
2. Ignoring the medical standards until the end. Vision requirements for the flying branch disqualify a large number of otherwise strong candidates, and refractive surgery like LASIK is disqualifying for the Air Force. Read the medical standards before you apply, not after you clear the written exam.
3. Guessing freely in the General Ability Test. At about 1.33 marks deducted per wrong answer against 2.5 for a correct one, loose guessing across 30 uncertain questions can cost more than it gains.
4. Treating the SSB as an afterthought. It carries 900 of the 1800 marks, and the gap between the written and final cutoffs shows exactly how much it decides.
5. Missing the age window. The 16.5 to 19.5 band is narrow and has no relaxation for any category, so a candidate typically gets only two or three attempts in total.
6. Letting one paper slide. The 25 per cent per-subject minimum means a strong Maths score cannot rescue a weak General Ability Test.

## How to apply for NDA

Applications go through the UPSC online portal, and the process is the same in every cycle.

1. Complete the One Time Registration on upsconline.nic.in if you have not already. This is a separate step from the application itself and is reused across UPSC exams.
2. Open the NDA and NA application when the notification goes live and fill in personal, educational, and communication details exactly as they appear on your Class 10 certificate.
3. Choose your wing preferences in order, keeping the PCM requirement in mind for Navy, Air Force, and Naval Academy.
4. Pick your exam centre. Centres fill on a first-apply basis, so applying early gives you a better chance of a nearby centre.
5. Upload your photograph and signature in the specified format, along with a photo ID.
6. Pay the fee of Rs 100. Women candidates and SC and ST candidates pay nothing.
7. Submit, then save the PDF and the registration number. UPSC opens a short correction window after the deadline for limited edits.

## Documents you will need

Keep these ready for the application and the SSB.

1. Your Class 10 and Class 12 certificates and mark sheets, with the wing-specific subjects.
2. Proof of date of birth, usually your Class 10 certificate.
3. A recent photograph, signature, and a valid photo ID matching your application.
4. Documents for any regional height relaxation and other certificates as listed in the notification.

## Frequently asked questions

**Can girls apply for NDA in 2026?**
Yes. Following a Supreme Court order in 2021, unmarried women are eligible for the NDA across all wings, that is the Army, Navy, Air Force, and Naval Academy, with the first women cadets admitted from the 2022 intake. In NDA II 2026, 24 of the 394 seats are earmarked for women.

**What is the NDA 2026 exam date?**
The NDA II 2026 written exam was scheduled for 13 September 2026. The earlier NDA I 2026 written exam was held on 12 April 2026. UPSC conducts the NDA and NA examination twice a year, as NDA I and NDA II.

**Is PCM compulsory for NDA?**
It depends on the wing. Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics are mandatory for the Navy, Air Force, and Naval Academy wings. The Army wing accepts any stream, so an Arts or Commerce candidate can join the Army wing without PCM but not the Navy or Air Force.

**What is the age limit for NDA 2026?**
Candidates must be between 16.5 and 19.5 years and unmarried, with the exact birth-date window set for each cycle in the notification. There is no age relaxation for any category.

**Do NDA cadets get a salary during training?**
Not a full salary. Cadets get free food, accommodation, uniforms, and medical care during training, and a stipend of around Rs 56,100 a month applies in the final pre-commission training year. A full officer package, with basic pay, Military Service Pay, and allowances, begins only on commissioning.

**What is the total marks of the NDA exam?**
The NDA selection carries 1800 marks in total: the written exam is 900 marks (Mathematics 300 plus General Ability Test 600), and the SSB interview is 900 marks. The final merit is built from both together.

**Is there negative marking in NDA?**
Yes. The Mathematics paper deducts about 0.83 marks for each wrong answer, and the General Ability Test deducts about 1.33 marks per wrong answer. Because the GAT penalty is heavier, blind guessing there is costlier than in Maths.

**Can I join NDA after 12th with Arts or Commerce?**
Yes, but only the Army wing. The Army wing accepts any stream, so Arts and Commerce candidates qualify. The Navy, Air Force, and Naval Academy wings require Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics.

**What is the difference between NDA and CDS?**
NDA is the officer entry straight after Class 12, at 16.5 to 19.5 years, while CDS is the graduate route into the armed forces at about 19 to 25 years. Both use a written exam plus the SSB interview, but NDA is the earlier entry and CDS is for graduates.

## SSC JE 2026 notification: 1,748 posts, applications close 22 September

The SSC JE 2026 notification came out on 2 September 2026 for 1,748 tentative vacancies, and the application window on ssc.gov.in closes at 11:00 pm on 22 September 2026. Fee payment stays open one day longer, until 11:00 pm on 23 September 2026. SSC has told candidates not to wait for the closing day, because the portal slows under load in the final hours.

Two disciplines are new to this cycle. Junior Engineer (Telecom) appears for the Department of Telecommunications, and the notification also carries Scientific Assistant posts in the India Meteorological Department, which is not a Junior Engineer post at all but is recruited through the same examination. A diploma holder in electronics or telecommunications who skipped SSC JE in earlier cycles now has a route that did not exist in 2024.

SSC Junior Engineer recruits Group B non-gazetted engineers into central government departments: the Border Roads Organisation, Brahmaputra Board, Central Water Commission, Central Public Works Department, Military Engineer Services, Farakka Barrage Project, the National Technical Research Organisation, the Directorate General of Lighthouses and Lightships, the Department of Telecommunications and the India Meteorological Department.

## SSC JE 2026 important dates

| Event | Date |
|---|---|
| Notification released | 2 September 2026 |
| Application window | 2 to 22 September 2026, closing 11:00 pm |
| Last date for fee payment | 23 September 2026, 11:00 pm |
| Application correction window | 28 to 30 September 2026 |
| Paper 1 (CBT) | October or November 2026, tentative |
| Paper 2 (CBT) | December 2026, tentative |

Only the application dates are firm. SSC gives Paper 1 and Paper 2 as tentative months in the notification and confirms the actual dates later through a separate exam notice on ssc.gov.in.

The correction window is worth a note of its own. It opens on 28 September, six days after applications close, and runs three days. SSC charges a correction fee and allows a limited number of corrections, so a candidate who notices a wrong discipline or department preference after submitting has that window and nothing after it.

## Vacancy details

SSC has notified 1,748 tentative vacancies for SSC JE 2026. The department-wise and branch-wise split had not been published when this page was last checked on 22 September 2026, and SSC marks the distribution as to be announced in the notification itself.

| Item | Figure |
|---|---|
| SSC JE 2026 tentative vacancies | 1,748 |
| SSC JE 2024 vacancies (previous cycle) | 1,731 |
| Discipline-wise split for 2026 | Not yet published by SSC |

The word tentative matters here. SSC revises the count once user departments confirm their indents, and the final figure has moved in both directions in past cycles. Any page giving you a confident Civil or Electrical number for 2026 today has made it up, because SSC has not released one.

## Participating departments

SSC JE fills posts across roughly nine central organisations, and the mix of disciplines differs by department.

| Department | Disciplines recruited |
|---|---|
| Central Public Works Department (CPWD) | Civil, Electrical |
| Central Water Commission (CWC) | Civil, Mechanical |
| Military Engineer Services (MES) | Civil, Electrical, Mechanical |
| Border Roads Organisation (BRO) | Civil, Electrical, Mechanical |
| Farakka Barrage Project | Civil, Electrical |
| Brahmaputra Board | Civil |
| National Technical Research Organisation (NTRO) | Civil |
| Central Water and Power Research Station | Electrical |
| Directorate of Quality Assurance (Naval) | Mechanical, Electrical |

## Eligibility: where a diploma is enough

This is the part candidates most often get wrong. The qualification bar genuinely varies by department, and a three-year diploma is enough for several posts.

| Department | Minimum qualification |
|---|---|
| CPWD (Civil, Electrical) | Diploma in the relevant engineering discipline |
| CWC (Civil) | Three-year diploma in Civil Engineering |
| CWC (Mechanical) | Degree or diploma in Mechanical Engineering |
| MES | Degree, or three-year diploma plus 2 years' experience |
| BRO | Degree, or three-year diploma plus 2 years' experience |

The rule to remember is simple. A three-year diploma is enough for several posts, notably in CPWD and CWC Civil. Some posts, especially in BRO and MES, need either a degree or a diploma backed by two years of relevant experience. Read the department column of the notification against your own qualification before you apply.

## Age limit and relaxation

Most SSC JE posts set an upper age of 30 years, while some CPWD posts allow up to 32 years. The exact limit is post-specific and printed in the notification. Standard relaxation applies: 3 years for OBC, 5 years for SC and ST, 10 years for PwBD, and 3 years for ex-servicemen over and above the upper limit.

## Application fee

| Category | Fee |
|---|---|
| General, OBC | Rs 100 |
| SC, ST, PwBD, ex-servicemen | Nil |
| All women candidates | Nil |

Payment is online through BHIM UPI, net banking, or a card.

## Selection process

SSC JE selection runs through two computer based papers followed by verification stages.

1. Paper 1 (CBT): objective, common to all candidates.
2. Paper 2 (CBT): a single-discipline technical paper.
3. Document verification.
4. Medical examination.

The final merit is built from the combined Paper 1 and Paper 2 marks. There is no interview.

## Paper 1 exam pattern

Paper 1 is a 200-mark objective test of two hours, with a penalty of 0.25 marks for each wrong answer.

| Section | Questions | Marks |
|---|---|---|
| General Intelligence and Reasoning | 50 | 50 |
| General Awareness | 50 | 50 |
| General Engineering (Civil or Electrical or Mechanical) | 100 | 100 |
| Total | 200 | 200 |

You attempt the General Engineering section only in the discipline you applied for, so a Civil applicant answers Civil questions and never sees the Electrical or Mechanical sets. Paper 1 is the screening stage that decides who moves on to the technical Paper 2, and it is common to both the degree and diploma holders who apply.

## Paper 2 exam pattern

Paper 2 is a 300-mark discipline paper of two hours, and it now runs in computer based mode. Watch the negative marking here.

| Feature | Detail |
|---|---|
| Total marks | 300 |
| Discipline | Civil and Structural, or Electrical, or Mechanical |
| Duration | 2 hours |
| Negative marking | 1 mark per wrong answer |

That negative-marking gap matters. Paper 1 penalises a quarter mark per error, but Paper 2 penalises a full mark, so blind guessing in the technical paper is far more costly. Many candidates who clear Paper 1 comfortably lose ground in Paper 2 by over-attempting.

## Syllabus

General Intelligence and Reasoning covers analogies, similarities and differences, space visualisation, problem solving, decision making, visual memory, relationship concepts, and arithmetical reasoning. General Awareness covers current events, India and its neighbours, history, culture, geography, the economic scene, general polity, and scientific research. Take a worked example in a metro (X-class city). On a basic of Rs 35,400, dearness allowance at 60 percent adds Rs 21,240, house rent allowance at the metro rate of 27 percent adds about Rs 9,558, and transport allowance with DA adds roughly Rs 5,400. That is a gross near Rs 71,600, and after the National Pension System contribution and other deductions the in-hand lands close to Rs 62,000 a month. In a Y-class city the HRA drops to about 18 percent and the in-hand settles a little lower. Many competitor pages still show a stale 17 to 50 percent DA, which undercounts the real figure.

Cut-offs vary by discipline, and Electrical and Mechanical usually close higher than Civil. As a reference from the SSC JE 2024 Paper 1 result, the unreserved cut-off sat near 122.93 for Civil and near 132.07 for Electrical and Mechanical.

| Category | Civil (2024) | Electrical / Mechanical (2024) |
|---|---|---|
| Unreserved | about 122.93 | about 132.07 |
| OBC | about 116.82 | slightly below UR |
| EWS | about 109.20 | varies |
| SC | about 101.85 | varies |
| ST | about 97.83 | varies |

Treat these as a planning band for 2026 and read the exact figures from the SSC JE 2026 result when it is published.

SSC JE gives an all-India Group B posting across central departments, which can mean transfers far from home but a wider promotion field. Most confusion around SSC JE comes down to one question: can I apply with only a diploma? The honest answer is that it depends on the department, and getting this wrong wastes an attempt. The catch is the field-heavy departments. BRO and several MES posts want either a degree or a diploma backed by two years of relevant work experience, because the roles carry more site responsibility. |---|---|---|
| Conducting body | Staff Selection Commission | Railway Recruitment Board |
| Pay Level | Level 6 (Rs 35,400 to 1,12,400) | Level 6 (same scale) |
| Group | Group B | Group C |
| Departments | CPWD, MES, CWC, BRO and others | Indian Railways only |
| Exam cycle | Annual | Irregular |
| Work nature | Site and office, desk-heavy in some departments | Field and maintenance heavy |

1. A recent passport-size photograph and a scanned signature in the SSC-specified format.
2. Your engineering degree or diploma certificate and mark sheets for the qualification and date-of-birth details.
3. An experience certificate, if you apply for a post that needs a diploma plus two years' experience.
4. A category certificate (OBC, SC, ST, EWS, or PwBD) where you claim relaxation.
5. Aadhaar or another government photo ID for the One Time Registration.

2. Open the SSC JE 2026 application and select your discipline, which must match the diploma or degree you hold.
3. Set your post and department preferences in order, since allocation follows this order and the list cannot be changed after the correction window shuts on 30 September.
4. Upload the photograph and signature in the formats the notification specifies.
5. Pay the Rs 100 fee. Women, SC, ST, PwBD and eligible ex-servicemen candidates are exempt.
6. Submit, then save the final printout and the payment receipt.

Paper 1 is given as October or November 2026 and Paper 2 as December 2026, both tentative.

1,748 tentative vacancies, against 1,731 in the 2024 cycle. No. SSC JE selection is Paper 1, then Paper 2, then document verification and a medical examination. The final merit rests on the combined Paper 1 and Paper 2 marks.

Most SSC JE posts set an upper age of 30 years, with some CPWD posts allowing up to 32, before relaxation of 3 years for OBC, 5 years for SC and ST, and 10 years for PwBD candidates.

## SBI Clerk 2026: 9,766 posts, prelims on 26 and 27 September

The SBI Clerk 2026 preliminary examination falls on 26 and 27 September 2026, in four shifts a day, and SBI released the prelims call letter on 21 September 2026. The recruitment runs under advertisement CRPD/CR/2026-27/17 for Junior Associate (Customer Support and Sales) in the clerical cadre, and applications ran from 11 to 31 August 2026.

The advertised count is 9,766 posts: 7,680 regular vacancies, which the detailed advertisement on sbi.bank.in breaks down state by state and category by category, and 2,086 backlog vacancies listed separately. That separation matters more than it looks. Backlog vacancies are reserved posts carried forward from earlier cycles that went unfilled, they are open only to the categories they were carried forward for, and SBI schedules them on their own track rather than merging them into the regular merit list.

Junior Associate stays one of the most applied-for jobs in the country because it asks only for a graduation, has no interview at any stage, and pays a working salary from the first month. What it asks in return is a local language you can be tested on, which is the condition that catches out more candidates than the written papers do.

## SBI Clerk 2026 important dates

| Event | Date |
|---|---|
| Advertisement CRPD/CR/2026-27/17 | August 2026 |
| Application window | 11 to 31 August 2026 |
| Prelims call letter | 21 September 2026 |
| Preliminary examination | 26 and 27 September 2026, four shifts a day |
| Main examination | November 2026 |
| Local Language Proficiency Test | After the main examination result |

The gap between prelims and mains is about eight weeks, which is the window that decides this recruitment. Prelims marks do not carry into the final merit, so a candidate who clears on 27 September starts level with everyone else and has those eight weeks to build the data interpretation, financial awareness and computer aptitude depth the mains tests.

## Vacancy details

| Category of vacancy | Posts |
|---|---|
| Regular vacancies | 7,680 |
| Backlog vacancies | 2,086 |
| Total advertised | 9,766 |
