## Namo Shetkari Maha Samman Nidhi Yojana 2026 at a glance

Namo Shetkari Maha Samman Nidhi Yojana is Maharashtra's state top-up to the central PM-Kisan Samman Nidhi. Every eligible Maharashtra farmer who receives Rs 6,000 per year from PM-Kisan gets an additional Rs 6,000 per year from the state government. The total is Rs 12,000 per year, disbursed as six installments of Rs 2,000 each (three from PM-Kisan, three from Namo Shetkari), all credited via Direct Benefit Transfer to the same Aadhaar-seeded bank account.

The scheme was cleared by the Maharashtra Cabinet on 30 May 2023 and formalised through Government Resolution number Kisani-2023/CR 42/11 A dated 15 June 2023 by the Agriculture Department. The first installment landed in October 2023. As of the 8th installment, released on 25 March 2026, the state has transferred Rs 1,768 crore to about 84 lakh farmers in a single release (per the Agriculture Minister Dattatray Bharane's press briefing and Krishi Jagran coverage). Cumulative disbursal across eight installments now stands at roughly Rs 16,000 crore.

Application is not required. If you are on the PM-Kisan beneficiary list and your PM-Kisan payment credits successfully, the Namo Shetkari payment follows automatically. The state pulls the eligibility snapshot from PM-Kisan and pays the corresponding farmer on the same or the very next installment cycle. The dedicated portal is nsmny.mahait.org where farmers can log in, verify beneficiary status, download the village-wise list, and file grievances.

The 9th installment is overdue and Maharashtra has still not announced a date. The trigger it normally follows, the PM-Kisan 23rd instalment, was released on 20 June 2026, and the state has gone more than three months without matching it. That is a long gap against the roughly 12 days the state achieved on the 8th installment. Local revenue offices in Vidarbha and Marathwada were asked to reconcile pending eKYC and land-record discrepancies before the release, and no payout date has followed.

## Installment history: eight releases from October 2023 to March 2026

Here is the full disbursal record so far. The pattern is roughly three installments a year, timed to follow each PM-Kisan installment by two to four weeks.

| Installment | Release date | Amount (approx.) | Beneficiary count | Reference |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1st | 27 October 2023 | Rs 1,720 cr | 85 lakh | Launch event, PM Modi and CM Shinde |
| 2nd | 15 January 2024 | Rs 1,680 cr | 82 lakh | Krishi Vibhag portal |
| 3rd | 29 February 2024 | Rs 1,691 cr | 84 lakh | Election-cycle release |
| 4th | 5 June 2024 | Rs 1,700 cr | 84 lakh | Post-Lok Sabha |
| 5th | 5 October 2024 | Rs 1,675 cr | 83 lakh | Ahead of Vidhan Sabha polls |
| 6th | 2 December 2024 | Rs 1,760 cr | 84 lakh | Post-election special |
| 7th | 25 November 2025 | Rs 1,755 cr | 84 lakh | Winter session announcement |
| 8th | 25 March 2026 | Rs 1,768 cr | 84 lakh | Krishi Jagran, Bharane briefing |

Nine cycles in about two-and-a-half years means the scheme has been delivered on a fairly reliable cadence, which is unusual for state top-ups that tend to slip during election years. The 8th installment came about 12 days after PM-Kisan's 22nd installment (released 13 March 2026 by Prime Minister Modi from Sitapur, Uttar Pradesh). That gap is the shortest lag on record and is a sign the state has cleaned its bank-seeding pipeline.

## PM-Kisan and Namo Shetkari: why both credit into the same account

The two schemes look separate on paper but function as one payment for the farmer. PM-Kisan is the central scheme run by the Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture, Government of India. Namo Shetkari is a Maharashtra-only add-on run by the Krishi Vibhag (Agriculture Department), Government of Maharashtra. Both use the same eligibility list, the same bank account, and the same DBT rails.

Here is how the two compare on the details that matter to a farmer.

| Attribute | PM-Kisan | Namo Shetkari |
|---|---|---|
| Level | Central | Maharashtra state |
| Annual benefit | Rs 6,000 | Rs 6,000 |
| Installments per year | 3 (Apr-Jul, Aug-Nov, Dec-Mar) | 3 (paid 2-4 weeks after each PM-Kisan installment) |
| Amount per installment | Rs 2,000 | Rs 2,000 |
| Portal | pmkisan.gov.in | nsmny.mahait.org |
| Application required | Yes (one-time, then eKYC every 3-6 months) | No (auto-inherits PM-Kisan list) |
| Nodal ministry | Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, GoI | Krishi Vibhag, Maharashtra |
| eKYC required | Yes (Aadhaar OTP or biometric at CSC) | No separate eKYC (inherits from PM-Kisan) |

The single most useful thing to understand is this. If the PM-Kisan installment credits into your bank account, the Namo Shetkari installment will follow within two to four weeks. If PM-Kisan does not credit, Namo Shetkari will not credit either. Fixing a Namo Shetkari failure almost always means fixing a PM-Kisan failure first.

## Eligibility in plain language

The scheme is open to all farmer families in Maharashtra who are already receiving PM-Kisan. Eligibility rides on the PM-Kisan list rather than a separate application form. That said, three specific groups of farmers who receive PM-Kisan do not automatically receive Namo Shetkari, and a few more categories are excluded from both.

To qualify:

- The farmer family (husband, wife, minor children as one unit) must own cultivable land recorded on the 7/12 extract or equivalent in Maharashtra.
- The land record must be digitised on the Mahabhulekh or e-Peek Pahani portal so the state can cross-verify.
- The Aadhaar of the applicant must be seeded to a working bank account and the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) mapping must be active.
- eKYC on the PM-Kisan portal must be current (redone every six months for most farmers, more often if flagged by the ministry).

Who is excluded, even if they own land in Maharashtra:

- All institutional landholders (companies, trusts, cooperative societies).
- Income tax payers in the last assessment year (self or any family member).
- Serving or retired government or PSU employees above Group D (Group C included in some circulars, this is worth confirming with the local Talathi).
- Sitting or former MPs, MLAs, MLCs, mayors, or chairpersons of Zilla Parishads.
- Registered professionals: doctors, engineers, lawyers, chartered accountants, architects practising in their profession.
- Recipients of a pension of Rs 10,000 or more per month (except SCS retired employees).
- Tenant farmers without registered land ownership (a long-standing gap the state has said it will address, still open as of July 2026).

If you meet PM-Kisan eligibility but are being denied Namo Shetkari specifically, the most common cause is that your name appears in the state's income-tax filer flag or the state has not yet ingested your recent land purchase into its 7/12 database.

## Worked example: Ramesh Patil, Ahmednagar, 2.4 hectares

Meet a hypothetical but realistic beneficiary. Ramesh Patil is 42, farms 2.4 hectares of rain-fed jowar and pigeon-pea in Kopargaon taluka, Ahmednagar district. He holds a Bank of Maharashtra savings account in Kopargaon branch with account number ending 4521, Aadhaar seeded and NPCI-mapped as of April 2024.

Here is what Ramesh receives in a full financial year (April 2025 to March 2026 payment cycle).

| Month | Scheme | Amount | Cumulative |
|---|---|---|---|
| June 2025 | PM-Kisan 20th installment | Rs 2,000 | Rs 2,000 |
| July 2025 | Namo Shetkari 6th installment (delayed) | Rs 2,000 | Rs 4,000 |
| October 2025 | PM-Kisan 21st installment | Rs 2,000 | Rs 6,000 |
| November 2025 | Namo Shetkari 7th installment | Rs 2,000 | Rs 8,000 |
| March 2026 | PM-Kisan 22nd installment | Rs 2,000 | Rs 10,000 |
| March 2026 | Namo Shetkari 8th installment | Rs 2,000 | Rs 12,000 |

Ramesh's account balance grew by Rs 12,000 in six DBT credits across the year, with the SMS from his Bank of Maharashtra account clearly showing "DBT-KRISHI" or "DBT-PMKISAN" in the transaction narration. That is the total combined benefit for a small farmer in Maharashtra as of the 2025-26 cycle. For a family with land in the name of both spouses, the payments are made to whichever spouse's name is on the primary landholding record, not doubled.

## Beneficiary status check on nsmny.mahait.org (step by step)

The official portal for checking Namo Shetkari status is nsmny.mahait.org, run by the Maharashtra Information Technology Corporation Limited (MahaIT) on behalf of the Agriculture Department. The steps are the same on mobile and desktop.

1. Open nsmny.mahait.org in your browser. The homepage is in Marathi and English (click "English" in the top right if the interface loads in Marathi).
2. Click "Beneficiary Status" in the top navigation. This opens a form at nsmny.mahait.org/Beneficiary_Status/Beneficiary.
3. Enter either your registered mobile number OR your PM-Kisan registration number. Only one is needed.
4. Enter the OTP that lands on the registered mobile within 30 seconds.
5. The status screen shows: current installment status (Paid / Pending / Rejected), the amount, the transaction reference number, the bank account (last four digits), and the credit date.

If your name is missing entirely from the portal, that means your PM-Kisan record has not yet been mirrored into the state database. This usually happens for new PM-Kisan enrolments (up to 60 days lag) or for records where the name spelling on Aadhaar and the 7/12 extract does not match. In either case, the fix is at the Talathi (village revenue officer) office, not at MahaIT.

To download the village-wise beneficiary list, click "Beneficiary List" on the homepage, then select District, then Taluka, then Village. The list is a downloadable PDF with all paid, pending, and rejected beneficiaries for that village against the latest installment. This is the same list your Gram Sevak keeps on file.

## Seven reasons the installment did not credit

Here is the diagnostic table our editorial team built after cross-referencing the top rejection reasons cited on the PM-Kisan portal, the MahaIT support helpline, and the Talathi grievance registers in Nashik and Ahmednagar. If your Namo Shetkari installment did not credit, one of these seven is almost certainly the reason.

| Flag | What it means | How to fix |
|---|---|---|
| eKYC pending on PM-Kisan | Your last Aadhaar OTP eKYC on pmkisan.gov.in has expired (six-month cycle). | Redo eKYC on the PM-Kisan portal or at the nearest CSC. Wait one full installment cycle. |
| Aadhaar-bank NPCI seeding failed | Your bank has your Aadhaar on record but the NPCI mapper has not been activated. | Visit your bank branch, ask for Aadhaar-NPCI seeding form, sign, submit. Confirmation SMS within 48 hours. |
| Name mismatch (Aadhaar vs 7/12) | Spelling of your name on Aadhaar and land record differs. | Get the 7/12 corrected at Talathi office (small fee, 15-30 days). |
| Land record not digitised | Your 7/12 has not been ingested into Mahabhulekh or e-Peek Pahani. | File request at Bhulekh office. Some talukas run camps quarterly. |
| Income tax filer flag | You (or spouse) filed an ITR in the last assessment year. | If ITR was filed in error and you had no taxable income, file NIL revised ITR and appeal at Krishi office. |
| Government employee in family | A spouse or adult family member is a serving/retired govt or PSU staff above Group D. | Not correctable. Ineligibility is by scheme design. |
| Institutional landholder tag | Land is held in the name of a trust, cooperative, or company. | Not correctable while the record stays institutional. |

The first four flags account for roughly 85 percent of all grievances filed at the MahaIT helpline (per an internal MahaIT sample cited in the March 2026 Bharane briefing). The last three are structural exclusions and cannot be waived at the district level.

## Documents required and Aadhaar-bank seeding

You do not need to submit any documents to receive Namo Shetkari once you are on the PM-Kisan list. But you should have the following ready for the one-time PM-Kisan registration (which is the actual gate).

- Aadhaar card of the applicant.
- 7/12 extract (Satbara Utara) of the cultivable land in the applicant's name.
- 8-A extract (village form 8-A, showing landowner status).
- Bank passbook or a cancelled cheque of the account where DBT should credit.
- Passport-size photograph.
- Mobile number (for OTP and installment SMS).

The Aadhaar-bank seeding is the single failure point that trips up the largest number of farmers. Seeding means two separate things that both need to be true. First, your bank has your Aadhaar number on file and printed on your passbook. Second, NPCI has been told by your bank to send Aadhaar-based DBT credits to this specific account. Farmers who have accounts at multiple banks (one Bank of Maharashtra, one cooperative, one Post Office) need to nominate exactly one for DBT, and that nomination is done by the bank, not by the farmer directly. If you have not visited your bank branch and specifically asked for "Aadhaar-NPCI seeding for DBT" in the last 12 months, do that first.

## What changed in 2026: the 8th installment and the 9th installment tracker

Two things changed materially in the 2026 cycle. First, the 8th installment credited on 25 March 2026 with Rs 1,768 crore going to about 84 lakh farmers, the largest single tranche the scheme has released so far (per Krishi Jagran, 26 March 2026 and confirmed by Agriculture Minister Dattatray Bharane in a state Vidhan Bhavan briefing). Second, the state closed the gap between the PM-Kisan release and the Namo Shetkari release to about 12 days, down from the 30-45 days that had been typical earlier. The tightening came from a MahaIT effort to pre-reconcile pending eKYC and NPCI cases in the weeks before each central release.

The 9th installment is being tracked here.

- Expected window on the historical cadence: June to July 2026, now passed.
- Actual release date as of 22 September 2026: not announced.
- Trigger: the PM-Kisan 23rd instalment, which was released on 20 June 2026 from Tarakeswar in West Bengal.
- Gap since the trigger: more than three months, against about 12 days on the 8th installment.
- Signal to watch: the state cabinet agenda in the last week of any month, or a release from the Krishi Vibhag handle @agrimahagov.

The length of that gap is the story here. Maharashtra had been tightening the delay between the central release and its own top-up, and the 9th installment has broken that pattern. When it lands, the date, amount and beneficiary count go into the installment history table above.

## How to raise a grievance

If your Namo Shetkari installment did not credit and none of the seven diagnostic flags above matches your case, the escalation path is:

1. First, check your PM-Kisan status at pmkisan.gov.in > Beneficiary Status. If PM-Kisan itself did not credit, fix that first (Namo Shetkari will not credit ahead of PM-Kisan).
2. Call the Namo Shetkari helpline at the state Krishi Vibhag on 020-25537041 (Mon-Sat, 10 am to 6 pm).
3. Visit the Taluka Krishi Adhikari office with your Aadhaar, 7/12 extract, and bank passbook. Ask for the DBT grievance register. Get your entry acknowledged with a token number.
4. If the taluka office does not resolve within 30 days, escalate to the District Superintending Agriculture Officer (Zilla Krishi Adhikari).
5. Portal grievance: log a complaint on Aaple Sarkar (aaplesarkar.mahaonline.gov.in) under Krishi > Namo Shetkari. Response is required within 21 working days by law.

Do not pay a middleman for status check or grievance filing. The portal and helpline are free.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is Namo Shetkari Maha Samman Nidhi Yojana?

It's Maharashtra's state top-up to the central PM-Kisan scheme. Every eligible Maharashtra farmer on the PM-Kisan list receives an additional Rs 6,000 per year in three installments of Rs 2,000, credited via DBT to the same bank account as PM-Kisan.

### How much money do farmers get under Namo Shetkari Yojana?

Rs 6,000 per year from Namo Shetkari, on top of Rs 6,000 per year from PM-Kisan. Total combined benefit is Rs 12,000 per year, disbursed as six installments of Rs 2,000 each across three PM-Kisan release cycles.

### When will the 9th installment of Namo Shetkari Yojana be released?

Maharashtra has not announced a date as of 22 September 2026, and the installment is overdue. Namo Shetkari normally follows the PM-Kisan release by 12 to 30 days, and the PM-Kisan 23rd instalment came on 20 June 2026, so the 9th installment is now more than three months past its usual trigger. Watch nsmny.mahait.org and the state cabinet agenda rather than a countdown on an aggregator page.

### Do I need to apply separately for Namo Shetkari if I get PM-Kisan?

No. The state pulls the eligibility list from PM-Kisan and pays the corresponding Maharashtra farmer automatically. There is no separate application form or eKYC required for Namo Shetkari.

### How can I check my Namo Shetkari beneficiary status?

Visit nsmny.mahait.org, click Beneficiary Status, enter your registered mobile number or PM-Kisan registration number, and enter the OTP. The status screen shows the current installment amount, transaction reference, credit date, and bank account (last four digits).

### Why did I not receive the Namo Shetkari 8th installment?

The seven most common reasons are: pending eKYC on PM-Kisan portal, failed Aadhaar-NPCI bank seeding, name mismatch between Aadhaar and 7/12 extract, undigitised land record, income tax filer flag, government employee in family, or institutional landholder tag. The first four are fixable at the Talathi or bank branch level.

### What is the difference between PM-Kisan and Namo Shetkari Yojana?

PM-Kisan is a central scheme run by the Government of India, giving Rs 6,000 per year to eligible farmers nationwide. Namo Shetkari is a Maharashtra-only add-on run by the state government, giving an additional Rs 6,000 per year to the same Maharashtra farmers. Both use the same eligibility list and bank account.

### Is eKYC mandatory for Namo Shetkari Yojana?

Not separately. But your PM-Kisan eKYC must be current, since Namo Shetkari inherits eligibility from PM-Kisan. Redo PM-Kisan eKYC every six months on pmkisan.gov.in or at the nearest CSC.

### Can tenant farmers get Namo Shetkari benefits?

Not at present. Only landowners with the land recorded on the 7/12 extract in their name are eligible. Tenant farmers without registered ownership are excluded, a gap the state has said it will address, still open as of July 2026.

### How to download the Namo Shetkari beneficiary list village-wise?

Go to nsmny.mahait.org, click Beneficiary List, select District, then Taluka, then Village. Download the PDF of all paid, pending, and rejected beneficiaries for that village against the latest installment.

### What documents are required for Namo Shetkari Yojana?

None separately. For the underlying PM-Kisan registration you need: Aadhaar card, 7/12 extract, 8-A extract, bank passbook or cancelled cheque, passport photo, and a working mobile number.

### Who is not eligible for Namo Shetkari Yojana?

Institutional landholders, income tax payers (self or any family member), serving or retired government or PSU employees above Group D, sitting or former elected representatives, registered professionals (doctors, engineers, lawyers, CAs, architects) practising in their profession, and pensioners receiving Rs 10,000 or more per month (with some exceptions). Tenant farmers without registered land ownership are also currently excluded.

## Sources

Primary sources.

- Namo Shetkari official portal: https://nsmny.mahait.org
- Beneficiary status page: https://nsmny.mahait.org/Beneficiary_Status/Beneficiary
- Government Resolution: No. Kisani-2023/CR 42/11 A dated 15 June 2023, Krishi Vibhag, Government of Maharashtra
- PM-Kisan portal: https://pmkisan.gov.in
- MahaDBT umbrella: https://mahadbt.maharashtra.gov.in
- Krishi Vibhag Maharashtra: https://krishi.maharashtra.gov.in
- Aaple Sarkar grievance portal: https://aaplesarkar.mahaonline.gov.in

Secondary sources.

- Krishi Jagran, 26 March 2026: "PM Modi releases additional Rs 2,000 crore to Maharashtra farmers under Namo Shetkari" (8th installment coverage).
- Agriculture Minister Dattatray Bharane's Vidhan Bhavan briefing, March 2026 (Rs 1,768 cr / 84 lakh beneficiary figure).
- Schemes in India, "Namo Shetkari Maha Samman Nidhi Yojana Maharashtra" (installment-by-installment tracker).
- Sarkari Yojana, "Namo Shetkari beneficiary list village-wise" (status check walkthrough).

Meet a hypothetical but realistic beneficiary. Ramesh Patil is 42, farms 2.4 hectares of rain-fed jowar and pigeon-pea in Kopargaon taluka, Ahmednagar district. He holds a Bank of Maharashtra savings account in Kopargaon branch with account number ending 4521, Aadhaar seeded and NPCI-mapped as of April 2024.

Here is what Ramesh receives in a full financial year (April 2025 to March 2026 payment cycle).

| Month | Scheme | Amount | Cumulative |
|---|---|---|---|
| June 2025 | PM-Kisan 20th installment | Rs 2,000 | Rs 2,000 |
| July 2025 | Namo Shetkari 6th installment (delayed) | Rs 2,000 | Rs 4,000 |
| October 2025 | PM-Kisan 21st installment | Rs 2,000 | Rs 6,000 |
| November 2025 | Namo Shetkari 7th installment | Rs 2,000 | Rs 8,000 |
| March 2026 | PM-Kisan 22nd installment | Rs 2,000 | Rs 10,000 |
| March 2026 | Namo Shetkari 8th installment | Rs 2,000 | Rs 12,000 |

Ramesh's account balance grew by Rs 12,000 in six DBT credits across the year, with the SMS from his Bank of Maharashtra account clearly showing "DBT-KRISHI" or "DBT-PMKISAN" in the transaction narration. That is the total combined benefit for a small farmer in Maharashtra as of the 2025-26 cycle. For a family with land in the name of both spouses, the payments are made to whichever spouse's name is on the primary landholding record, not doubled.

## Beneficiary status check on nsmny.mahait.org (step by step)

The official portal for checking Namo Shetkari status is nsmny.mahait.org, run by the Maharashtra Information Technology Corporation Limited (MahaIT) on behalf of the Agriculture Department. The steps are the same on mobile and desktop.

1. Open nsmny.mahait.org in your browser. The homepage is in Marathi and English (click "English" in the top right if the interface loads in Marathi).
2. Click "Beneficiary Status" in the top navigation. This opens a form at nsmny.mahait.org/Beneficiary_Status/Beneficiary.
3. Enter either your registered mobile number OR your PM-Kisan registration number. Only one is needed.
4. Enter the OTP that lands on the registered mobile within 30 seconds.
5. The status screen shows: current installment status (Paid / Pending / Rejected), the amount, the transaction reference number, the bank account (last four digits), and the credit date.

If your name is missing entirely from the portal, that means your PM-Kisan record has not yet been mirrored into the state database. This usually happens for new PM-Kisan enrolments (up to 60 days lag) or for records where the name spelling on Aadhaar and the 7/12 extract does not match. In either case, the fix is at the Talathi (village revenue officer) office, not at MahaIT.

To download the village-wise beneficiary list, click "Beneficiary List" on the homepage, then select District, then Taluka, then Village. The list is a downloadable PDF with all paid, pending, and rejected beneficiaries for that village against the latest installment. This is the same list your Gram Sevak keeps on file.

## Seven reasons the installment did not credit

Here is the diagnostic table our editorial team built after cross-referencing the top rejection reasons cited on the PM-Kisan portal, the MahaIT support helpline, and the Talathi grievance registers in Nashik and Ahmednagar. If your Namo Shetkari installment did not credit, one of these seven is almost certainly the reason.

| Flag | What it means | How to fix |
|---|---|---|
| eKYC pending on PM-Kisan | Your last Aadhaar OTP eKYC on pmkisan.gov.in has expired (six-month cycle). | Redo eKYC on the PM-Kisan portal or at the nearest CSC. Wait one full installment cycle. |
| Aadhaar-bank NPCI seeding failed | Your bank has your Aadhaar on record but the NPCI mapper has not been activated. | Visit your bank branch, ask for Aadhaar-NPCI seeding form, sign, submit. Confirmation SMS within 48 hours. |
| Name mismatch (Aadhaar vs 7/12) | Spelling of your name on Aadhaar and land record differs. | Get the 7/12 corrected at Talathi office (small fee, 15-30 days). |
| Land record not digitised | Your 7/12 has not been ingested into Mahabhulekh or e-Peek Pahani. | File request at Bhulekh office. Some talukas run camps quarterly. |
| Income tax filer flag | You (or spouse) filed an ITR in the last assessment year. | If ITR was filed in error and you had no taxable income, file NIL revised ITR and appeal at Krishi office. |
| Government employee in family | A spouse or adult family member is a serving/retired govt or PSU staff above Group D. | Not correctable. Ineligibility is by scheme design. |
| Institutional landholder tag | Land is held in the name of a trust, cooperative, or company. | Not correctable while the record stays institutional. |

The first four flags account for roughly 85 percent of all grievances filed at the MahaIT helpline (per an internal MahaIT sample cited in the March 2026 Bharane briefing). The last three are structural exclusions and cannot be waived at the district level.

## Documents required and Aadhaar-bank seeding

You do not need to submit any documents to receive Namo Shetkari once you are on the PM-Kisan list. But you should have the following ready for the one-time PM-Kisan registration (which is the actual gate).

- Aadhaar card of the applicant.
- 7/12 extract (Satbara Utara) of the cultivable land in the applicant's name.
- 8-A extract (village form 8-A, showing landowner status).
- Bank passbook or a cancelled cheque of the account where DBT should credit.
- Passport-size photograph.
- Mobile number (for OTP and installment SMS).

The Aadhaar-bank seeding is the single failure point that trips up the largest number of farmers. Seeding means two separate things that both need to be true. First, your bank has your Aadhaar number on file and printed on your passbook. Second, NPCI has been told by your bank to send Aadhaar-based DBT credits to this specific account. Farmers who have accounts at multiple banks (one Bank of Maharashtra, one cooperative, one Post Office) need to nominate exactly one for DBT, and that nomination is done by the bank, not by the farmer directly. If you have not visited your bank branch and specifically asked for "Aadhaar-NPCI seeding for DBT" in the last 12 months, do that first.

## What changed in 2026: the 8th installment and the 9th installment tracker

Two things changed materially in the 2026 cycle. First, the 8th installment credited on 25 March 2026 with Rs 1,768 crore going to about 84 lakh farmers, the largest single tranche the scheme has released so far (per Krishi Jagran, 26 March 2026 and confirmed by Agriculture Minister Dattatray Bharane in a state Vidhan Bhavan briefing). Second, the state closed the gap between the PM-Kisan release and the Namo Shetkari release to about 12 days, down from the 30-45 days that had been typical earlier. The tightening came from a MahaIT effort to pre-reconcile pending eKYC and NPCI cases in the weeks before each central release.

The 9th installment is being tracked here.

- Expected window: June to July 2026 (based on the historical 3-4 month cadence).
- Actual release date as of 24 July 2026: not yet announced.
- Trigger: PM-Kisan 23rd installment (release date also pending as of 24 July 2026).
- Signal to watch: state cabinet agenda in the last week of any month, or a press release from the Krishi Vibhag Twitter handle @agrimahagov.

We update this section within 24 hours of any 9th installment credit. If you landed on this page after the 9th installment has released, the date, amount, and beneficiary count will be listed in the installment history table above.

## How to raise a grievance

If your Namo Shetkari installment did not credit and none of the seven diagnostic flags above matches your case, the escalation path is:

1. First, check your PM-Kisan status at pmkisan.gov.in > Beneficiary Status. If PM-Kisan itself did not credit, fix that first (Namo Shetkari will not credit ahead of PM-Kisan).
2. Call the Namo Shetkari helpline at the state Krishi Vibhag on 020-25537041 (Mon-Sat, 10 am to 6 pm).
3. Visit the Taluka Krishi Adhikari office with your Aadhaar, 7/12 extract, and bank passbook. Ask for the DBT grievance register. Get your entry acknowledged with a token number.
4. If the taluka office does not resolve within 30 days, escalate to the District Superintending Agriculture Officer (Zilla Krishi Adhikari).
5. Portal grievance: log a complaint on Aaple Sarkar (aaplesarkar.mahaonline.gov.in) under Krishi > Namo Shetkari. Response is required within 21 working days by law.

Do not pay a middleman for status check or grievance filing. The portal and helpline are free.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is Namo Shetkari Maha Samman Nidhi Yojana?

It's Maharashtra's state top-up to the central PM-Kisan scheme. Every eligible Maharashtra farmer on the PM-Kisan list receives an additional Rs 6,000 per year in three installments of Rs 2,000, credited via DBT to the same bank account as PM-Kisan.

### How much money do farmers get under Namo Shetkari Yojana?

Rs 6,000 per year from Namo Shetkari, on top of Rs 6,000 per year from PM-Kisan. Total combined benefit is Rs 12,000 per year, disbursed as six installments of Rs 2,000 each across three PM-Kisan release cycles.

### When will the 9th installment of Namo Shetkari Yojana be released?

As of 24 July 2026, the state has not announced an official date. Based on the historical 3-4 month cadence, the 9th installment is expected between June and July 2026. It typically follows the PM-Kisan release by 12 to 30 days.

### Do I need to apply separately for Namo Shetkari if I get PM-Kisan?

No. The state pulls the eligibility list from PM-Kisan and pays the corresponding Maharashtra farmer automatically. There is no separate application form or eKYC required for Namo Shetkari.

### How can I check my Namo Shetkari beneficiary status?

Visit nsmny.mahait.org, click Beneficiary Status, enter your registered mobile number or PM-Kisan registration number, and enter the OTP. The status screen shows the current installment amount, transaction reference, credit date, and bank account (last four digits).

### Why did I not receive the Namo Shetkari 8th installment?

The seven most common reasons are: pending eKYC on PM-Kisan portal, failed Aadhaar-NPCI bank seeding, name mismatch between Aadhaar and 7/12 extract, undigitised land record, income tax filer flag, government employee in family, or institutional landholder tag. The first four are fixable at the Talathi or bank branch level.

### What is the difference between PM-Kisan and Namo Shetkari Yojana?

PM-Kisan is a central scheme run by the Government of India, giving Rs 6,000 per year to eligible farmers nationwide. Namo Shetkari is a Maharashtra-only add-on run by the state government, giving an additional Rs 6,000 per year to the same Maharashtra farmers. Both use the same eligibility list and bank account.

### Is eKYC mandatory for Namo Shetkari Yojana?

Not separately. But your PM-Kisan eKYC must be current, since Namo Shetkari inherits eligibility from PM-Kisan. Redo PM-Kisan eKYC every six months on pmkisan.gov.in or at the nearest CSC.

### Can tenant farmers get Namo Shetkari benefits?

Not at present. Only landowners with the land recorded on the 7/12 extract in their name are eligible. Tenant farmers without registered ownership are excluded, a gap the state has said it will address, still open as of July 2026.

### How to download the Namo Shetkari beneficiary list village-wise?

Go to nsmny.mahait.org, click Beneficiary List, select District, then Taluka, then Village. Download the PDF of all paid, pending, and rejected beneficiaries for that village against the latest installment.

### What documents are required for Namo Shetkari Yojana?

None separately. For the underlying PM-Kisan registration you need: Aadhaar card, 7/12 extract, 8-A extract, bank passbook or cancelled cheque, passport photo, and a working mobile number.

### Who is not eligible for Namo Shetkari Yojana?

Institutional landholders, income tax payers (self or any family member), serving or retired government or PSU employees above Group D, sitting or former elected representatives, registered professionals (doctors, engineers, lawyers, CAs, architects) practising in their profession, and pensioners receiving Rs 10,000 or more per month (with some exceptions). Tenant farmers without registered land ownership are also currently excluded.

## Sources

Primary sources.

- Namo Shetkari official portal: https://nsmny.mahait.org
- Beneficiary status page: https://nsmny.mahait.org/Beneficiary_Status/Beneficiary
- Government Resolution: No. Kisani-2023/CR 42/11 A dated 15 June 2023, Krishi Vibhag, Government of Maharashtra
- PM-Kisan portal: https://pmkisan.gov.in
- MahaDBT umbrella: https://mahadbt.maharashtra.gov.in
- Krishi Vibhag Maharashtra: https://krishi.maharashtra.gov.in
- Aaple Sarkar grievance portal: https://aaplesarkar.mahaonline.gov.in

Secondary sources.

- Krishi Jagran, 26 March 2026: "PM Modi releases additional Rs 2,000 crore to Maharashtra farmers under Namo Shetkari" (8th installment coverage).
- Agriculture Minister Dattatray Bharane's Vidhan Bhavan briefing, March 2026 (Rs 1,768 cr / 84 lakh beneficiary figure).
- Schemes in India, "Namo Shetkari Maha Samman Nidhi Yojana Maharashtra" (installment-by-installment tracker).
- Sarkari Yojana, "Namo Shetkari beneficiary list village-wise" (status check walkthrough).

## RRB Group D 2026: the CBT is over and the answer key is out

RRB Group D 2026, advertised as CEN 09/2025, fills 22,195 Level 1 posts in Indian Railways. Its Computer Based Test ran from 3 to 25 August 2026 across 16 days, in three shifts a day at more than 200 centres, and the Railway Recruitment Boards published the provisional answer key on 7 September 2026. The objection window that followed it has closed.

What is left is the result, which the RRBs have not dated. Normalisation can only be applied once every shift is accounted for, so the result is expected towards the end of October 2026 rather than in September. The admit card was released from 31 July 2026 and the city intimation slip from 24 July 2026, both on rrbapply.gov.in and the regional RRB websites.

This is one of the largest recruitment exercises anywhere. Reported applicant figures vary widely across sources, from around 58 lakh to close to a crore, and the exact number is not something any secondary site can confirm. Either way, 22,195 posts against a field that size means the Computer Based Test is decided on a handful of marks, and the negative marking on this paper is the reason many candidates lose them.

## The CBT schedule as it ran

The Railway Recruitment Board revised this schedule once during the cycle. These are the days the exam was held on.

| Week | Dates in August 2026 |
|---|---|
| First | 3, 4, 5, 6 |
| Second | 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14 |
| Third | 17, 18, 19, 20, 21 |
| Fourth | 25 |

Sixteen days, three shifts each, which means a large number of distinct question papers. Because of that, RRB applies normalisation across shifts, so your final score is adjusted for the relative difficulty of the paper you sat rather than taken as a raw total. A candidate who gets a harder shift is not penalised for it, and equally a raw score from an easier shift does not carry the advantage it appears to.

## Why you are seeing two sets of contradictory dates

Search for RRB Group D right now and you will find pages announcing that the CBT is starting alongside pages announcing that PET dates are out and results have been declared. Both are accurate. They describe different recruitment cycles.

| Cycle | Stage in September 2026 |
|---|---|
| CEN 08/2024 | Result declared, at the Physical Efficiency Test and later stages |
| CEN 09/2025 | CBT completed 25 August 2026, answer key out, result awaited |

If you applied in the current round, yours is CEN 09/2025 and the result is your live stage. The PET notices circulating now belong to the earlier cycle and do not apply to you. Check the CEN number on your admit card if you are unsure, because acting on the wrong cycle's notice is the most common avoidable error in railway recruitment.

## Exam day: what to carry and what to expect

Take the printed admit card and the original photo identity document whose details you entered in your application. RRB is strict on the identity document matching the application, and a mismatch is grounds for being turned away.

Reach the centre by the reporting time on the admit card, not the exam start time. Gates close well before the paper begins, and RRB does not admit latecomers. Biometric verification and document checks take time, which is why the reporting window opens so far ahead.

Electronic items are prohibited: mobile phones, smart watches, calculators, Bluetooth devices and any storage media. So are bags, written material and, at most centres, metallic items and jewellery. Centres do not reliably provide storage, so carry as little as possible.

The paper is 90 minutes, extended to 120 minutes for candidates with a disability who have been granted a scribe or compensatory time.

## Exam pattern

The CBT is a single objective paper of 100 questions.

| Section | Questions | Marks |
|---|---|---|
| General Intelligence and Reasoning | 30 | 30 |
| Mathematics | 25 | 25 |
| General Science | 25 | 25 |
| General Awareness and Current Affairs | 20 | 20 |
| Total | 100 | 100 |

Duration is 90 minutes. Each correct answer carries 1 mark, and one third of a mark is deducted for each wrong answer.

That negative marking deserves attention, because several other recruitments carry none and the habits do not transfer. Work the arithmetic. A correct answer gains 1, a wrong one costs 0.33. Guessing blindly among four options gives you one correct and three wrong on average, so 1 minus 0.99, which is essentially break-even with added variance and no real gain. Eliminate one option and the odds tilt in your favour. Eliminate two and answering is clearly correct.

The practical rule: answer everything you know or can narrow to two options, and leave alone the questions where you have no basis at all. Candidates who carry an attempt-everything habit from exams like UP Police or Bihar Police, where there is no penalty, hand back marks here.

## Qualifying marks

Clearing the paper requires a minimum percentage that varies by category, commonly applied as 40 per cent for unreserved and EWS candidates, 30 per cent for OBC and SC, and 25 per cent for ST, with relaxation for candidates with disabilities where there is a shortfall.

Meeting that minimum is not selection. It makes you eligible to be ranked, and the actual shortlisting for the PET is done on normalised merit against the vacancy position in your region, which sits far above the qualifying floor.

## Syllabus

The paper is pitched at Class 10 level and rewards coverage more than depth.

Reasoning carries the most questions at 30 and covers analogies, series completion, coding and decoding, mathematical operations, relationships, syllogism, Venn diagrams, data interpretation, statement and conclusion, directions and analytical reasoning. It is the most trainable section, since the question types repeat and practice converts directly into speed.

Mathematics covers number systems, decimals and fractions, LCM and HCF, ratio and proportion, percentages, mensuration, time and work, time and distance, simple and compound interest, profit and loss, algebra, geometry and trigonometry basics, elementary statistics, and age and calendar problems.

General Science covers physics, chemistry and life sciences at Class 10 level. Physics and chemistry tend to carry more weight than biology in recent papers.

General Awareness and Current Affairs covers science and technology, sports, culture, personalities, economics, politics and general current affairs, with a bias towards the last year and towards railway-related developments.

## What the Level 1 posts actually are

Level 1 covers six categories of post, and they are different jobs despite sharing an entry route.

Pointsman operates points and signals at stations and yards, a safety-critical outdoor role often on night shifts. Track Maintainer Grade IV maintains the permanent way, which is physically demanding outdoor work on the track itself. Assistant posts in the Loco Shed, in Operations, and in TL and AC support maintenance and operations in depots and on trains. The remaining assistant categories cover workshop and departmental support roles.

Post preference is exercised during the application and allocation follows merit, region and vacancy position. Almost all of these involve shift work, outdoor conditions and a physical component, which is why the recruitment carries a Physical Efficiency Test at all.

## Physical Efficiency Test

The PET is pass or fail. It adds no marks to your merit position, and failing it removes you regardless of your CBT score.

| Candidates | Lifting and carrying | Running |
|---|---|---|
| Male | 35 kg carried over 100 metres in under 2 minutes, in one go without setting it down | 1000 metres in 4 minutes 15 seconds |
| Female | 20 kg carried over 100 metres in under 2 minutes, in one go without setting it down | 1000 metres in 5 minutes 40 seconds |

The lifting event is the one candidates underestimate, and the condition attached to it is what makes it hard: the weight has to be carried the full 100 metres in a single attempt without being put down. That is a grip strength and carrying endurance problem more than a maximal strength one, and it is not something general gym work prepares you for specifically. Loaded carries, farmer's walks and grip work are the training that transfers.

The running standard is more forgiving. 1000 metres in 4 minutes 15 seconds for men works out to about 4 minutes 15 seconds per kilometre, which is demanding but well short of the 800 metre standards in state police recruitment.

Both events are attempted in sequence and both must be cleared.

## Selection process

| Stage | Role |
|---|---|
| Computer Based Test | Decides merit, after normalisation across shifts |
| Physical Efficiency Test | Qualifying only |
| Document Verification | Eligibility check |
| Medical Examination | Fitness against the medical standard for the post |

The medical standard varies by post, and it is stricter than candidates expect for safety-related categories. Vision requirements for Pointsman and other safety posts in particular rule out candidates who would pass the standard for a clerical role, so check the medical classification for the posts you have preferenced.

## Salary of an RRB Group D employee

Level 1 of the 7th Pay Commission matrix carries a basic pay of Rs 18,000 a month, with an annual increment of about Rs 500 at the entry stage.

On top of basic pay come dearness allowance at the prevailing rate, house rent allowance at 8, 16 or 24 per cent of basic depending on the classification of your posting city, transport allowance, and railway-specific allowances including running or shift allowances where the post attracts them. Taking those together, in-hand pay at entry commonly works out in the region of Rs 22,500 to Rs 25,380 a month depending on posting and the current DA rate.

The non-cash side matters in railway service more than in most government jobs. Railway quarters where available, the free or concessional pass entitlement for the employee and family, railway medical facilities through railway hospitals, and pension benefits under the applicable rules all carry real value that the headline figure understates.

## Career progression

Level 1 is the entry rung and progression runs through departmental channels.

| Stage | Route |
|---|---|
| Level 1 entry post | Direct recruitment |
| Level 2 and 3 | Departmental promotion and departmental examinations |
| Higher technical and supervisory grades | Selection posts through departmental examination |

Indian Railways runs an internal promotion system with a defined quota of higher posts filled from serving employees through the General Departmental Competitive Examination and other departmental routes. A Level 1 entrant who prepares for those examinations can move up materially over a career, and many technical supervisors began at this level.

## How to use the remaining exam days

Because the CBT runs to 25 August, a large share of candidates still have days or weeks before they sit it, and that time is better spent on the paper's specific demands than on fresh study.

Reasoning is where the marginal marks are. It carries the most questions at 30, the question types repeat across cycles, and speed on them is a trained skill rather than a knowledge one. Working timed sets of past reasoning questions is the highest-return use of a remaining week.

Practise at the real pace. 100 questions in 90 minutes gives you 54 seconds per question, and the paper is not designed for careful deliberation on every item. Candidates lose more to poor time allocation, spending four minutes on a hard maths question, than to gaps in knowledge.

Rehearse the marking decision. Take a full mock, mark each answer as confident, narrowed to two, or pure guess, then score it both ways: once counting your guesses and once leaving them blank. Doing that twice tells you your own accuracy rate on narrowed questions, which is a better guide to exam-day behaviour than any general rule about negative marking.

Revise general science and current affairs last, since those are recall-heavy and benefit from being fresh.

## Eligibility

On age, the band for the cycle is set in the CEN, commonly 18 to 36 years for Level 1 posts with relaxation of 3 years for OBC, 5 years for SC and ST, and further relaxation for ex-servicemen and other specified categories.

On education, the requirement is Class 10 pass, or an ITI certificate from an institution recognised by NCVT or SCVT, or an equivalent National Apprenticeship Certificate. A Class 10 pass alone is sufficient for most Level 1 posts.

On medical fitness, each post carries a medical classification and candidates must meet the standard for the post allotted, with vision requirements being the most common ground for rejection in safety categories.

## What happens after the CBT

The last shift was held on 25 August 2026 and the provisional answer key came out on 7 September 2026, with objections closing after it. The result follows once normalisation is applied across every shift, which the RRBs have not dated and which past cycles put at roughly two months after the final shift.

Shortlisted candidates are called for the PET, then document verification, then the medical. Use the intervening period rather than waiting on the result. The lifting standard in particular takes weeks of specific training to build, and candidates who begin only after the shortlist is published arrive underprepared for an event that is pass or fail.

Keep your documents ready in the meantime: Class 10 certificate, ITI or NAC certificate where relied on, category certificate in the central government format with a current non-creamy layer certificate for OBC candidates, and the identity documents matching your application.

## Frequently asked questions

**When is the RRB Group D 2026 exam?**
The Computer Based Test for CEN 09/2025 runs across 16 days in August 2026: the 3rd, 4th, 5th, 6th, 9th, 10th, 11th, 12th, 13th, 14th, 17th, 18th, 19th, 20th, 21st and 25th, in three shifts a day at more than 200 centres. The schedule was revised, so rely on the date printed on your admit card rather than an earlier notice.

**How do I download the RRB Group D admit card 2026?**
Admit cards were released from 31 July 2026 on rrbapply.gov.in and the regional Railway Recruitment Board websites, four days before the first exam date. The city intimation slip, which tells you your exam city ahead of the admit card, was released from 24 July 2026. Log in with your registration number and date of birth.

**Is there negative marking in RRB Group D?**
Yes. One third of a mark is deducted for each wrong answer, against 1 mark for a correct one. Blind guessing among four options is roughly break-even and adds variance, so answer where you know the answer or can narrow it to two options, and leave the rest. This differs from several state police recruitments that carry no penalty, and the habits do not transfer.

**How many vacancies are in RRB Group D 2026?**
There are 22,195 Level 1 vacancies under CEN 09/2025, covering Pointsman, Track Maintainer Grade IV, Assistant Loco Shed, Assistant Operations, Assistant TL and AC, and other assistant categories. Reported applicant numbers vary between about 58 lakh and close to a crore across sources.

**What is the RRB Group D exam pattern?**
One objective Computer Based Test of 100 questions for 100 marks in 90 minutes, extended to 120 minutes for eligible candidates with a disability. The split is General Intelligence and Reasoning 30, Mathematics 25, General Science 25, and General Awareness and Current Affairs 20. One third of a mark is deducted per wrong answer, and scores are normalised across shifts.

**What are the RRB Group D PET standards?**
Male candidates must carry 35 kg over 100 metres in under 2 minutes without setting the weight down, and run 1000 metres in 4 minutes 15 seconds. Female candidates must carry 20 kg over 100 metres in under 2 minutes on the same condition, and run 1000 metres in 5 minutes 40 seconds. The PET is qualifying only and adds no marks to merit, but failing it ends the attempt.

**What is the salary of an RRB Group D employee?**
Level 1 of the 7th CPC matrix carries a basic pay of Rs 18,000 a month. With dearness allowance, house rent allowance at 8 to 24 per cent by city class, transport allowance and railway allowances, in-hand pay at entry is commonly about Rs 22,500 to Rs 25,380 depending on posting and the current DA rate. Railway quarters where available, the travel pass entitlement and railway medical facilities add substantial non-cash value.

**What are the qualifying marks for RRB Group D?**
The minimum is commonly 40 per cent for unreserved and EWS candidates, 30 per cent for OBC and SC candidates and 25 per cent for ST candidates, with relaxation for candidates with disabilities where there is a shortfall. Meeting the minimum only makes you eligible to be ranked. Shortlisting for the PET is done on normalised merit against the vacancy position in your region, which sits well above the qualifying floor.

**Why do some sites say RRB Group D PET dates are out while others say the CBT is starting?**
Because two cycles are live at the same time. CEN 08/2024 has had its result declared and is at the Physical Efficiency Test and later stages, while CEN 09/2025 is the cycle whose Computer Based Test runs from 3 to 25 August 2026. Check the CEN number on your admit card to know which notices apply to you.

**What is the educational qualification for RRB Group D?**
Class 10 pass from a recognised board, or an ITI certificate from an institution recognised by NCVT or SCVT, or an equivalent National Apprenticeship Certificate. A Class 10 pass alone is sufficient for most Level 1 posts, which makes this one of the most accessible central government recruitments by qualification.

**What is normalisation in the RRB Group D exam?**
Because the exam runs across 16 days in three shifts, many different question papers are used, and they are not equally difficult. RRB applies a normalisation formula that adjusts raw scores for the relative difficulty of the shift a candidate sat. Your final score therefore differs from your raw score, and results can only be published once every shift has been conducted.

**What documents should I carry to the RRB Group D exam?**
The printed admit card and the original photo identity document whose details match your application. RRB is strict on that match. Mobile phones, smart watches, calculators, Bluetooth devices, storage media, bags and written material are prohibited, and most centres also bar metallic items and jewellery. Arrive by the reporting time on the admit card rather than the exam start time, since gates close well before the paper begins.

## RRB Group D 2026: the exam is running right now

RRB Group D 2026, advertised as CEN 09/2025, fills 22,195 Level 1 posts in Indian Railways, and its Computer Based Test began on 3 August 2026. The exam runs across 16 days through to 25 August 2026, in three shifts a day at more than 200 centres.

If you are sitting this exam, the two things you need are your admit card, released from 31 July 2026 on the Railway Recruitment Board portal, and your exam city, which came earlier through the city intimation slip from 24 July 2026. Both are downloaded from rrbapply.gov.in and the regional RRB websites.

This is one of the largest recruitment exercises anywhere. Reported applicant figures vary widely across sources, from around 58 lakh to close to a crore, and the exact number is not something any secondary site can confirm. Either way, 22,195 posts against a field that size means the Computer Based Test is decided on a handful of marks, and the negative marking on this paper is the reason many candidates lose them.

## The full CBT schedule

The Railway Recruitment Board revised the schedule, so check your admit card rather than an earlier notice. These are the announced exam days.

| Week | Dates in August 2026 |
|---|---|
| First | 3, 4, 5, 6 |
| Second | 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14 |
| Third | 17, 18, 19, 20, 21 |
| Fourth | 25 |

Sixteen days, three shifts each, which means a large number of distinct question papers. Because of that, RRB applies normalisation across shifts, so your final score is adjusted for the relative difficulty of the paper you sat rather than taken as a raw total. A candidate who gets a harder shift is not penalised for it, and equally a raw score from an easier shift does not carry the advantage it appears to.

## Why you are seeing two sets of contradictory dates

Search for RRB Group D right now and you will find pages announcing that the CBT is starting alongside pages announcing that PET dates are out and results have been declared. Both are accurate. They describe different recruitment cycles.

| Cycle | Stage as of August 2026 |
|---|---|
| CEN 08/2024 | Result declared, at the Physical Efficiency Test and later stages |
| CEN 09/2025 | Computer Based Test running 3 to 25 August 2026 |

If you applied in the current round, yours is CEN 09/2025 and the CBT is your live stage. The PET notices circulating now belong to the earlier cycle and do not apply to you. Check the CEN number on your admit card if you are unsure, because acting on the wrong cycle's notice is the most common avoidable error in railway recruitment.

## Exam day: what to carry and what to expect

Take the printed admit card and the original photo identity document whose details you entered in your application. RRB is strict on the identity document matching the application, and a mismatch is grounds for being turned away.

Reach the centre by the reporting time on the admit card, not the exam start time. Gates close well before the paper begins, and RRB does not admit latecomers. Biometric verification and document checks take time, which is why the reporting window opens so far ahead.

Electronic items are prohibited: mobile phones, smart watches, calculators, Bluetooth devices and any storage media. So are bags, written material and, at most centres, metallic items and jewellery. Centres do not reliably provide storage, so carry as little as possible.

The paper is 90 minutes, extended to 120 minutes for candidates with a disability who have been granted a scribe or compensatory time.

## Exam pattern

The CBT is a single objective paper of 100 questions.

| Section | Questions | Marks |
|---|---|---|
| General Intelligence and Reasoning | 30 | 30 |
| Mathematics | 25 | 25 |
| General Science | 25 | 25 |
| General Awareness and Current Affairs | 20 | 20 |
| Total | 100 | 100 |

Duration is 90 minutes. Each correct answer carries 1 mark, and one third of a mark is deducted for each wrong answer.

That negative marking deserves attention, because several other recruitments carry none and the habits do not transfer. Work the arithmetic. A correct answer gains 1, a wrong one costs 0.33. Guessing blindly among four options gives you one correct and three wrong on average, so 1 minus 0.99, which is essentially break-even with added variance and no real gain. Eliminate one option and the odds tilt in your favour. Eliminate two and answering is clearly correct.

The practical rule: answer everything you know or can narrow to two options, and leave alone the questions where you have no basis at all. Candidates who carry an attempt-everything habit from exams like UP Police or Bihar Police, where there is no penalty, hand back marks here.

## Qualifying marks

Clearing the paper requires a minimum percentage that varies by category, commonly applied as 40 per cent for unreserved and EWS candidates, 30 per cent for OBC and SC, and 25 per cent for ST, with relaxation for candidates with disabilities where there is a shortfall.

Meeting that minimum is not selection. It makes you eligible to be ranked, and the actual shortlisting for the PET is done on normalised merit against the vacancy position in your region, which sits far above the qualifying floor.

## Syllabus

The paper is pitched at Class 10 level and rewards coverage more than depth.

Reasoning carries the most questions at 30 and covers analogies, series completion, coding and decoding, mathematical operations, relationships, syllogism, Venn diagrams, data interpretation, statement and conclusion, directions and analytical reasoning. It is the most trainable section, since the question types repeat and practice converts directly into speed.

Mathematics covers number systems, decimals and fractions, LCM and HCF, ratio and proportion, percentages, mensuration, time and work, time and distance, simple and compound interest, profit and loss, algebra, geometry and trigonometry basics, elementary statistics, and age and calendar problems.

General Science covers physics, chemistry and life sciences at Class 10 level. Physics and chemistry tend to carry more weight than biology in recent papers.

General Awareness and Current Affairs covers science and technology, sports, culture, personalities, economics, politics and general current affairs, with a bias towards the last year and towards railway-related developments.

## What the Level 1 posts actually are

Level 1 covers six categories of post, and they are different jobs despite sharing an entry route.

Pointsman operates points and signals at stations and yards, a safety-critical outdoor role often on night shifts. Track Maintainer Grade IV maintains the permanent way, which is physically demanding outdoor work on the track itself. Assistant posts in the Loco Shed, in Operations, and in TL and AC support maintenance and operations in depots and on trains. The remaining assistant categories cover workshop and departmental support roles.

Post preference is exercised during the application and allocation follows merit, region and vacancy position. Almost all of these involve shift work, outdoor conditions and a physical component, which is why the recruitment carries a Physical Efficiency Test at all.

## Physical Efficiency Test

The PET is pass or fail. It adds no marks to your merit position, and failing it removes you regardless of your CBT score.

| Candidates | Lifting and carrying | Running |
|---|---|---|
| Male | 35 kg carried over 100 metres in under 2 minutes, in one go without setting it down | 1000 metres in 4 minutes 15 seconds |
| Female | 20 kg carried over 100 metres in under 2 minutes, in one go without setting it down | 1000 metres in 5 minutes 40 seconds |

The lifting event is the one candidates underestimate, and the condition attached to it is what makes it hard: the weight has to be carried the full 100 metres in a single attempt without being put down. That is a grip strength and carrying endurance problem more than a maximal strength one, and it is not something general gym work prepares you for specifically. Loaded carries, farmer's walks and grip work are the training that transfers.

The running standard is more forgiving. 1000 metres in 4 minutes 15 seconds for men works out to about 4 minutes 15 seconds per kilometre, which is demanding but well short of the 800 metre standards in state police recruitment.

Both events are attempted in sequence and both must be cleared.

## Selection process

| Stage | Role |
|---|---|
| Computer Based Test | Decides merit, after normalisation across shifts |
| Physical Efficiency Test | Qualifying only |
| Document Verification | Eligibility check |
| Medical Examination | Fitness against the medical standard for the post |

The medical standard varies by post, and it is stricter than candidates expect for safety-related categories. Vision requirements for Pointsman and other safety posts in particular rule out candidates who would pass the standard for a clerical role, so check the medical classification for the posts you have preferenced.

## Salary of an RRB Group D employee

Level 1 of the 7th Pay Commission matrix carries a basic pay of Rs 18,000 a month, with an annual increment of about Rs 500 at the entry stage.

On top of basic pay come dearness allowance at the prevailing rate, house rent allowance at 8, 16 or 24 per cent of basic depending on the classification of your posting city, transport allowance, and railway-specific allowances including running or shift allowances where the post attracts them. Taking those together, in-hand pay at entry commonly works out in the region of Rs 22,500 to Rs 25,380 a month depending on posting and the current DA rate.

The non-cash side matters in railway service more than in most government jobs. Railway quarters where available, the free or concessional pass entitlement for the employee and family, railway medical facilities through railway hospitals, and pension benefits under the applicable rules all carry real value that the headline figure understates.

## Career progression

Level 1 is the entry rung and progression runs through departmental channels.

| Stage | Route |
|---|---|
| Level 1 entry post | Direct recruitment |
| Level 2 and 3 | Departmental promotion and departmental examinations |
| Higher technical and supervisory grades | Selection posts through departmental examination |

Indian Railways runs an internal promotion system with a defined quota of higher posts filled from serving employees through the General Departmental Competitive Examination and other departmental routes. A Level 1 entrant who prepares for those examinations can move up materially over a career, and many technical supervisors began at this level.

## How to use the remaining exam days

Because the CBT runs to 25 August, a large share of candidates still have days or weeks before they sit it, and that time is better spent on the paper's specific demands than on fresh study.

Reasoning is where the marginal marks are. It carries the most questions at 30, the question types repeat across cycles, and speed on them is a trained skill rather than a knowledge one. Working timed sets of past reasoning questions is the highest-return use of a remaining week.

Practise at the real pace. 100 questions in 90 minutes gives you 54 seconds per question, and the paper is not designed for careful deliberation on every item. Candidates lose more to poor time allocation, spending four minutes on a hard maths question, than to gaps in knowledge.

Rehearse the marking decision. Take a full mock, mark each answer as confident, narrowed to two, or pure guess, then score it both ways: once counting your guesses and once leaving them blank. Doing that twice tells you your own accuracy rate on narrowed questions, which is a better guide to exam-day behaviour than any general rule about negative marking.

Revise general science and current affairs last, since those are recall-heavy and benefit from being fresh.

## Eligibility

On age, the band for the cycle is set in the CEN, commonly 18 to 36 years for Level 1 posts with relaxation of 3 years for OBC, 5 years for SC and ST, and further relaxation for ex-servicemen and other specified categories.

On education, the requirement is Class 10 pass, or an ITI certificate from an institution recognised by NCVT or SCVT, or an equivalent National Apprenticeship Certificate. A Class 10 pass alone is sufficient for most Level 1 posts.

On medical fitness, each post carries a medical classification and candidates must meet the standard for the post allotted, with vision requirements being the most common ground for rejection in safety categories.

## What happens after the CBT

Results follow the completion of all shifts, and given the exam runs to 25 August 2026 the result will take time, since normalisation can only be applied once every shift has been conducted.

Shortlisted candidates are called for the PET, then document verification, then the medical. Use the intervening period rather than waiting on the result. The lifting standard in particular takes weeks of specific training to build, and candidates who begin only after the shortlist is published arrive underprepared for an event that is pass or fail.

Keep your documents ready in the meantime: Class 10 certificate, ITI or NAC certificate where relied on, category certificate in the central government format with a current non-creamy layer certificate for OBC candidates, and the identity documents matching your application.

## Frequently asked questions

**When is the RRB Group D 2026 exam?**
The Computer Based Test for CEN 09/2025 runs across 16 days in August 2026: the 3rd, 4th, 5th, 6th, 9th, 10th, 11th, 12th, 13th, 14th, 17th, 18th, 19th, 20th, 21st and 25th, in three shifts a day at more than 200 centres. The schedule was revised, so rely on the date printed on your admit card rather than an earlier notice.

**How do I download the RRB Group D admit card 2026?**
Admit cards were released from 31 July 2026 on rrbapply.gov.in and the regional Railway Recruitment Board websites, four days before the first exam date. The city intimation slip, which tells you your exam city ahead of the admit card, was released from 24 July 2026. Log in with your registration number and date of birth.

**Is there negative marking in RRB Group D?**
Yes. One third of a mark is deducted for each wrong answer, against 1 mark for a correct one. Blind guessing among four options is roughly break-even and adds variance, so answer where you know the answer or can narrow it to two options, and leave the rest. This differs from several state police recruitments that carry no penalty, and the habits do not transfer.

**How many vacancies are in RRB Group D 2026?**
There are 22,195 Level 1 vacancies under CEN 09/2025, covering Pointsman, Track Maintainer Grade IV, Assistant Loco Shed, Assistant Operations, Assistant TL and AC, and other assistant categories. Reported applicant numbers vary between about 58 lakh and close to a crore across sources.

**What is the RRB Group D exam pattern?**
One objective Computer Based Test of 100 questions for 100 marks in 90 minutes, extended to 120 minutes for eligible candidates with a disability. The split is General Intelligence and Reasoning 30, Mathematics 25, General Science 25, and General Awareness and Current Affairs 20. One third of a mark is deducted per wrong answer, and scores are normalised across shifts.

**What are the RRB Group D PET standards?**
Male candidates must carry 35 kg over 100 metres in under 2 minutes without setting the weight down, and run 1000 metres in 4 minutes 15 seconds. Female candidates must carry 20 kg over 100 metres in under 2 minutes on the same condition, and run 1000 metres in 5 minutes 40 seconds. The PET is qualifying only and adds no marks to merit, but failing it ends the attempt.

**What is the salary of an RRB Group D employee?**
Level 1 of the 7th CPC matrix carries a basic pay of Rs 18,000 a month. With dearness allowance, house rent allowance at 8 to 24 per cent by city class, transport allowance and railway allowances, in-hand pay at entry is commonly about Rs 22,500 to Rs 25,380 depending on posting and the current DA rate. Railway quarters where available, the travel pass entitlement and railway medical facilities add substantial non-cash value.

**What are the qualifying marks for RRB Group D?**
The minimum is commonly 40 per cent for unreserved and EWS candidates, 30 per cent for OBC and SC candidates and 25 per cent for ST candidates, with relaxation for candidates with disabilities where there is a shortfall. Meeting the minimum only makes you eligible to be ranked. Shortlisting for the PET is done on normalised merit against the vacancy position in your region, which sits well above the qualifying floor.

**Why do some sites say RRB Group D PET dates are out while others say the CBT is starting?**
Because two cycles are live at the same time. CEN 08/2024 has had its result declared and is at the Physical Efficiency Test and later stages, while CEN 09/2025 is the cycle whose Computer Based Test runs from 3 to 25 August 2026. Check the CEN number on your admit card to know which notices apply to you.

**What is the educational qualification for RRB Group D?**
Class 10 pass from a recognised board, or an ITI certificate from an institution recognised by NCVT or SCVT, or an equivalent National Apprenticeship Certificate. A Class 10 pass alone is sufficient for most Level 1 posts, which makes this one of the most accessible central government recruitments by qualification.

**What is normalisation in the RRB Group D exam?**
Because the exam runs across 16 days in three shifts, many different question papers are used, and they are not equally difficult. RRB applies a normalisation formula that adjusts raw scores for the relative difficulty of the shift a candidate sat. Your final score therefore differs from your raw score, and results can only be published once every shift has been conducted.

**What documents should I carry to the RRB Group D exam?**
The printed admit card and the original photo identity document whose details match your application. RRB is strict on that match. Mobile phones, smart watches, calculators, Bluetooth devices, storage media, bags and written material are prohibited, and most centres also bar metallic items and jewellery. Arrive by the reporting time on the admit card rather than the exam start time, since gates close well before the paper begins.
