## CAT 2026: registration closes 22 September at 5 pm

CAT 2026, the Common Admission Test for the IIMs and several hundred other business schools, is conducted this year by IIM Indore. Registration opened at 10:00 am on 3 August 2026 and closes at 5:00 pm on 22 September 2026, extended by a week from the original 15 September. The examination is on Sunday, 29 November 2026, in three slots across roughly 170 cities and more than 300 test centres.

The window shuts at 5:00 pm on 22 September 2026 and does not reopen. IIM Indore has said this extended date is final and there is no late-fee route after it. IIM Indore released the notification and information bulletin on 26 July 2026 on iimcat.ac.in.

Two things about CAT catch first-time candidates out, and both are structural rather than about difficulty. The sections are time-locked, so you cannot return to a section once its 40 minutes are gone. And a meaningful share of questions carry no negative marking at all, which changes how you should attempt them.

## Important dates

| Event | Date |
|---|---|
| Notification and information bulletin | 26 July 2026 |
| Registration opens | 3 August 2026, 10:00 am |
| Registration closes | 22 September 2026, 5:00 pm (extended from 15 September) |
| Admit card download | 4 November to 29 November 2026 |
| Examination | 29 November 2026, three slots |
| Result | Expected first week of January 2027 |

The gap between the close of registration and the examination is about ten weeks, which is the realistic preparation window for anyone starting now.

## Exam pattern

CAT is a computer based test of 68 questions over 120 minutes.

| Section | Questions | MCQ | TITA | Time |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Verbal Ability and Reading Comprehension (VARC) | 24 | 20 | 4 | 40 minutes |
| Data Interpretation and Logical Reasoning (DILR) | 22 | 11 | 11 | 40 minutes |
| Quantitative Ability (QA) | 22 | 14 | 8 | 40 minutes |
| Total | 68 | 45 | 23 | 120 minutes |

Sections appear in that fixed order and each is locked to its own 40 minutes. When the time for VARC expires the screen moves to DILR whether you are finished or not, and you cannot go back. Candidates used to exams where they can budget time freely across the whole paper find this the hardest adjustment.

## Marking, and why TITA changes your strategy

Every correct answer carries 3 marks. An incorrect multiple-choice answer costs 1 mark. TITA questions, meaning Type In The Answer, carry no negative marking at all.

That distinction is worth acting on deliberately. Of the 68 questions, 23 are TITA: 4 in VARC, 11 in DILR and 8 in QA. On those 23 there is no downside to attempting, so every one should carry an answer even if it is a considered guess. Leaving a TITA question blank is a guaranteed zero where a guess costs nothing.

On the 45 MCQs the arithmetic is different. A correct answer gains 3, a wrong one costs 1, so guessing blindly among four options gives on average one correct at plus 3 against three wrong at minus 3, which is exactly break-even with substantial variance. Eliminate one option and the odds turn positive. With no basis for elimination, leaving it is the sounder call.

Note the DILR section in particular: 11 of its 22 questions are TITA, half the section. A candidate who runs short of time there and leaves TITA questions blank is discarding free expected value.

## Eligibility

A bachelor's degree with at least 50 per cent marks or an equivalent CGPA is required, relaxed to 45 per cent for SC, ST and PwD candidates.

Candidates in the final year of their degree are eligible to apply and may be admitted provisionally, subject to producing proof of completion within the deadline set by the institute admitting them.

Holders of professional qualifications including CA, CS and ICWA are eligible on the same percentage conditions.

There is no age limit for CAT and no cap on the number of attempts. That is unusual among Indian competitive examinations and worth knowing: a candidate who does not get the score they want can simply sit it again the following year without any eligibility consequence.

## Registration fee

| Category | Fee |
|---|---|
| General, EWS and NC-OBC | Rs 2,700 |
| SC, ST and PwD | Rs 1,350 |

The fee is paid online during registration. Candidates select up to a defined number of preferred test cities in order during the application, and IIM Indore allots one of them, so ordering those preferences carefully matters if travel is a constraint.

## What the sections actually test

Verbal Ability and Reading Comprehension is dominated by reading comprehension, typically four passages accounting for the majority of the section, with the remainder covering para jumbles, para summary and odd sentence out. Notably, VARC in recent cycles has contained no direct grammar or vocabulary questions, which surprises candidates preparing from older material. The skill being tested is reading dense argumentative prose quickly and accurately.

Data Interpretation and Logical Reasoning consists of set-based questions, usually four or five sets of four to six questions each, covering tables, graphs, caselets, arrangements, distributions, games and tournaments. This is the section where set selection matters more than raw ability: choosing two solvable sets and completing them fully beats starting four and finishing none.

Quantitative Ability covers arithmetic, algebra, geometry and mensuration, number systems, and modern mathematics including permutations, combinations and probability. Arithmetic carries the heaviest weight in recent papers, covering percentages, ratio and proportion, averages and mixtures, time speed and distance, time and work, profit and loss, and simple and compound interest.

## Percentile, not marks

CAT results are reported as percentiles rather than raw scores, and the distinction matters when you set targets.

A percentile tells you the proportion of candidates who scored below you, not the proportion of marks you obtained. In a field of well over two lakh candidates, a raw score that looks modest in absolute terms can correspond to a high percentile, because the paper is designed so that no one comes close to attempting everything.

Sectional percentiles are also computed separately, and most institutes apply sectional cutoffs in addition to an overall one. A candidate with a strong overall percentile but a weak sectional percentile in one area can be filtered out by institutes that enforce sectional minimums, which is the argument against abandoning a weak section entirely.

Because CAT is normalised across three slots on the same day, your final score is adjusted for the relative difficulty of the slot you sat, so a harder slot is not a disadvantage.

## Which institutes accept CAT

The 21 Indian Institutes of Management use CAT for admission to their flagship postgraduate programmes, and several hundred other business schools accept the score, including FMS Delhi, SPJIMR, MDI Gurgaon, IMT Ghaziabad, IMI New Delhi and a large number of university departments and private institutes.

Selection at almost all of them combines the CAT percentile with academic record, work experience, and performance in a subsequent round involving written ability tests, group discussions and personal interviews. The percentile gets you the call; it does not by itself get you the seat. Weightage formulas differ by institute and are published in their admission policies, and several give explicit weight to academic consistency across Class 10, Class 12 and graduation, along with diversity factors.

## Preparing between now and 29 November

There are roughly 17 weeks from the opening of registration to the examination, which is a workable window for a serious start and a comfortable one for a candidate already preparing.

Begin with a full mock under real conditions to establish a baseline. Without one you are guessing at where your weaknesses lie, and CAT preparation is almost entirely about allocating limited time to the sections that will move your percentile most.

Build reading speed for VARC from the start, since it is the slowest capability to develop. Reading dense argumentative material daily, editorials and long-form journalism rather than exam passages alone, is what shifts comprehension speed over months.

Practise DILR by sets rather than by questions, and train the skill of scanning all available sets in the first two minutes and choosing which to attempt. That selection decision affects the score more than solving ability does.

Drill arithmetic in QA, since it carries the greatest weight and rewards accuracy and speed over sophisticated technique.

Take a full mock every week from September, and increase to two a week in November, spending as long analysing each mock as you spent writing it.

## CAT compared with the other MBA entrance exams

CAT is not the only route, and the calendar is arranged so that a candidate can sit several in one season. Most serious applicants do.

| Exam | Conducted by | Exam date | Duration and questions | Negative marking |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CAT 2026 | IIM Indore | 29 November 2026 | 120 min, 68 questions | 1 mark on MCQs only |
| XAT 2027 | XLRI Jamshedpur | 3 January 2027 | 180 min, 95 questions | 0.25, plus a penalty beyond 8 unattempted |
| SNAP 2026 | Symbiosis International | December 2026, multiple slots | 60 min, 60 questions | As per the SNAP bulletin |
| NMAT 2026 | Graduate Management Admission Council | 2 November to 20 December 2026 | 120 min, 108 questions | None |
| MAT | All India Management Association | Multiple cycles a year | As per the AIMA bulletin | As per the AIMA bulletin |

Three differences are worth planning around. XAT includes a decision making section that no other exam has, and it penalises leaving more than eight questions unattempted, which is a rule unique to it. NMAT allows multiple attempts within its window and lets you choose your section order, which suits candidates who perform better with a familiar sequence. SNAP is much shorter at 60 minutes, so it rewards speed over stamina.

Because the dates are spread from late November to early January, sitting three or four of these costs mainly registration fees and a few weekends, and it widens the set of institutes available to you considerably. Our pages on [XAT 2027](/entrance-exams/xat-2027), [SNAP 2026](/entrance-exams/snap-2026) and [NMAT 2026](/entrance-exams/nmat-2026) cover each in detail.

## What happens after the CAT result

A percentile is the beginning of the admission process rather than the end of it, and candidates focused entirely on the exam are often unprepared for what follows.

Institutes release shortlists in January and February based on the CAT percentile combined with their own weightage formula, which typically includes Class 10 and Class 12 marks, graduation performance, work experience and diversity factors. Two candidates with the same percentile can receive very different call sets because of academic record alone.

Shortlisted candidates attend a selection round, usually some combination of a Written Ability Test, a group discussion or group exercise, and a personal interview. The final offer is computed from a formula that gives the CAT percentile a defined weight alongside these components, and at several institutes the exam accounts for less than half of the final score.

This has a practical consequence for anyone reading this in August. Preparation for the interview stage, which means being able to discuss your own academic background, work, and reasons for an MBA coherently, is worth starting well before the result rather than in the fortnight after it.

## Mistakes that cost candidates marks

Ignoring the sectional time limit in practice. Candidates who take mocks without enforcing the 40-minute lock arrive on exam day with time-allocation habits that the software will not permit.

Leaving TITA questions blank. There are 23 of them carrying no penalty, and every blank one is a guaranteed zero in place of a free attempt.

Starting too many DILR sets. Completing two sets fully scores better than beginning four and finishing none, and set selection in the opening minutes is the highest-value decision in the section.

Abandoning a weak section entirely. Sectional percentiles are computed separately and most institutes enforce sectional cutoffs, so a zero-effort section can end an application that a strong overall percentile would otherwise carry.

Preparing VARC from grammar and vocabulary material. Recent papers test reading comprehension rather than rules, so the useful preparation is sustained reading of dense argumentative prose.

Taking mocks without analysing them. The analysis is where the improvement happens, and it deserves at least as much time as the attempt.

## How to apply

Applications are filed only on iimcat.ac.in.

1. Register with a valid email address and mobile number, both of which are used for all communication including the admit card.
2. Complete the application with academic details exactly as on your certificates, since percentages entered here feed institute shortlisting.
3. Select your programme preferences across the participating IIMs.
4. Choose your preferred test cities in order, since allotment follows that order and your travel plans depend on it.
5. Upload photograph and signature in the specified format and size.
6. Pay the fee of Rs 2,700, or Rs 1,350 for SC, ST and PwD candidates.
7. Submit and save the application, then download the admit card between 4 and 29 November 2026.

## Documents you will need

1. Class 10 and Class 12 mark sheets and certificates.
2. Graduation mark sheets and degree certificate, or a bonafide certificate if you are in the final year.
3. Category certificate in the prescribed central government format for NC-OBC, SC, ST and EWS claims, issued within the validity period stated in the bulletin.
4. PwD certificate where applicable.
5. Work experience certificates where you intend to claim experience at the interview stage.
6. Photograph, signature and a photo identity document matching the application.

## Frequently asked questions

**When is CAT 2026 and when does registration close?**
CAT 2026 is on Sunday, 29 November 2026, in three slots across roughly 170 cities. Registration opened at 10:00 am on 3 August 2026 and closes at 5:00 pm on 22 September 2026 on iimcat.ac.in, after IIM Indore extended the original 15 September deadline by a week. The IIMs have said this date is final and there is no late-fee route once it passes. IIM Indore is the conducting institute this year and released the notification on 26 July 2026. Admit cards are available from 4 November.

**What is the CAT 2026 exam pattern?**

The sections appear in that fixed order and you cannot return to a section once its time expires.

**What is the eligibility for CAT 2026?**
A bachelor's degree with at least 50 per cent marks or equivalent CGPA, relaxed to 45 per cent for SC, ST and PwD candidates. Final-year students may apply and be admitted provisionally. Professional qualifications including CA, CS and ICWA are accepted on the same percentage conditions. There is no age limit and no cap on the number of attempts.

**What is the CAT 2026 registration fee?**
Rs 2,700 for General, EWS and NC-OBC candidates and Rs 1,350 for SC, ST and PwD candidates, paid online during registration on iimcat.ac.in.

## CAT 2026: registration is open now

CAT 2026, the Common Admission Test for the IIMs and several hundred other business schools, is conducted this year by IIM Indore. Registration opened at 10:00 am on 3 August 2026 and closes at 5:00 pm on 22 September 2026, extended by a week from the original 15 September. The examination is on Sunday, 29 November 2026, in three slots across roughly 170 cities and more than 300 test centres.

If you intend to sit CAT this year, the window is open right now and it does not reopen. IIM Indore released the notification and information bulletin on 26 July 2026 on iimcat.ac.in.

Two things about CAT catch first-time candidates out, and both are structural rather than about difficulty. The sections are time-locked, so you cannot return to a section once its 40 minutes are gone. And a meaningful share of questions carry no negative marking at all, which changes how you should attempt them.

## Important dates

| Event | Date |
|---|---|
| Notification and information bulletin | 26 July 2026 |
| Registration opens | 3 August 2026, 10:00 am |
| Registration closes | 22 September 2026, 5:00 pm (extended from 15 September) |
| Admit card download | 4 November to 29 November 2026 |
| Examination | 29 November 2026, three slots |
| Result | Expected first week of January 2027 |

The gap between the close of registration and the examination is about ten weeks, which is the realistic preparation window for anyone starting now.

## Exam pattern

CAT is a computer based test of 68 questions over 120 minutes.

| Section | Questions | MCQ | TITA | Time |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Verbal Ability and Reading Comprehension (VARC) | 24 | 20 | 4 | 40 minutes |
| Data Interpretation and Logical Reasoning (DILR) | 22 | 11 | 11 | 40 minutes |
| Quantitative Ability (QA) | 22 | 14 | 8 | 40 minutes |
| Total | 68 | 45 | 23 | 120 minutes |

Sections appear in that fixed order and each is locked to its own 40 minutes. When the time for VARC expires the screen moves to DILR whether you are finished or not, and you cannot go back. Candidates used to exams where they can budget time freely across the whole paper find this the hardest adjustment.

## Marking, and why TITA changes your strategy

Every correct answer carries 3 marks. An incorrect multiple-choice answer costs 1 mark. TITA questions, meaning Type In The Answer, carry no negative marking at all.

That distinction is worth acting on deliberately. Of the 68 questions, 23 are TITA: 4 in VARC, 11 in DILR and 8 in QA. On those 23 there is no downside to attempting, so every one should carry an answer even if it is a considered guess. Leaving a TITA question blank is a guaranteed zero where a guess costs nothing.

On the 45 MCQs the arithmetic is different. A correct answer gains 3, a wrong one costs 1, so guessing blindly among four options gives on average one correct at plus 3 against three wrong at minus 3, which is exactly break-even with substantial variance. Eliminate one option and the odds turn positive. With no basis for elimination, leaving it is the sounder call.

Note the DILR section in particular: 11 of its 22 questions are TITA, half the section. A candidate who runs short of time there and leaves TITA questions blank is discarding free expected value.

## Eligibility

A bachelor's degree with at least 50 per cent marks or an equivalent CGPA is required, relaxed to 45 per cent for SC, ST and PwD candidates.

Candidates in the final year of their degree are eligible to apply and may be admitted provisionally, subject to producing proof of completion within the deadline set by the institute admitting them.

Holders of professional qualifications including CA, CS and ICWA are eligible on the same percentage conditions.

There is no age limit for CAT and no cap on the number of attempts. That is unusual among Indian competitive examinations and worth knowing: a candidate who does not get the score they want can simply sit it again the following year without any eligibility consequence.

## Registration fee

| Category | Fee |
|---|---|
| General, EWS and NC-OBC | Rs 2,700 |
| SC, ST and PwD | Rs 1,350 |

The fee is paid online during registration. Candidates select up to a defined number of preferred test cities in order during the application, and IIM Indore allots one of them, so ordering those preferences carefully matters if travel is a constraint.

## What the sections actually test

Verbal Ability and Reading Comprehension is dominated by reading comprehension, typically four passages accounting for the majority of the section, with the remainder covering para jumbles, para summary and odd sentence out. Notably, VARC in recent cycles has contained no direct grammar or vocabulary questions, which surprises candidates preparing from older material. The skill being tested is reading dense argumentative prose quickly and accurately.

Data Interpretation and Logical Reasoning consists of set-based questions, usually four or five sets of four to six questions each, covering tables, graphs, caselets, arrangements, distributions, games and tournaments. This is the section where set selection matters more than raw ability: choosing two solvable sets and completing them fully beats starting four and finishing none.

Quantitative Ability covers arithmetic, algebra, geometry and mensuration, number systems, and modern mathematics including permutations, combinations and probability. Arithmetic carries the heaviest weight in recent papers, covering percentages, ratio and proportion, averages and mixtures, time speed and distance, time and work, profit and loss, and simple and compound interest.

## Percentile, not marks

CAT results are reported as percentiles rather than raw scores, and the distinction matters when you set targets.

A percentile tells you the proportion of candidates who scored below you, not the proportion of marks you obtained. In a field of well over two lakh candidates, a raw score that looks modest in absolute terms can correspond to a high percentile, because the paper is designed so that no one comes close to attempting everything.

Sectional percentiles are also computed separately, and most institutes apply sectional cutoffs in addition to an overall one. A candidate with a strong overall percentile but a weak sectional percentile in one area can be filtered out by institutes that enforce sectional minimums, which is the argument against abandoning a weak section entirely.

Because CAT is normalised across three slots on the same day, your final score is adjusted for the relative difficulty of the slot you sat, so a harder slot is not a disadvantage.

## Which institutes accept CAT

The 21 Indian Institutes of Management use CAT for admission to their flagship postgraduate programmes, and several hundred other business schools accept the score, including FMS Delhi, SPJIMR, MDI Gurgaon, IMT Ghaziabad, IMI New Delhi and a large number of university departments and private institutes.

Selection at almost all of them combines the CAT percentile with academic record, work experience, and performance in a subsequent round involving written ability tests, group discussions and personal interviews. The percentile gets you the call; it does not by itself get you the seat. Weightage formulas differ by institute and are published in their admission policies, and several give explicit weight to academic consistency across Class 10, Class 12 and graduation, along with diversity factors.

## Preparing between now and 29 November

There are roughly 17 weeks from the opening of registration to the examination, which is a workable window for a serious start and a comfortable one for a candidate already preparing.

Begin with a full mock under real conditions to establish a baseline. Without one you are guessing at where your weaknesses lie, and CAT preparation is almost entirely about allocating limited time to the sections that will move your percentile most.

Build reading speed for VARC from the start, since it is the slowest capability to develop. Reading dense argumentative material daily, editorials and long-form journalism rather than exam passages alone, is what shifts comprehension speed over months.

Practise DILR by sets rather than by questions, and train the skill of scanning all available sets in the first two minutes and choosing which to attempt. That selection decision affects the score more than solving ability does.

Drill arithmetic in QA, since it carries the greatest weight and rewards accuracy and speed over sophisticated technique.

Take a full mock every week from September, and increase to two a week in November, spending as long analysing each mock as you spent writing it.

## CAT compared with the other MBA entrance exams

CAT is not the only route, and the calendar is arranged so that a candidate can sit several in one season. Most serious applicants do.

| Exam | Conducted by | Exam date | Duration and questions | Negative marking |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CAT 2026 | IIM Indore | 29 November 2026 | 120 min, 68 questions | 1 mark on MCQs only |
| XAT 2027 | XLRI Jamshedpur | 3 January 2027 | 180 min, 95 questions | 0.25, plus a penalty beyond 8 unattempted |
| SNAP 2026 | Symbiosis International | December 2026, multiple slots | 60 min, 60 questions | As per the SNAP bulletin |
| NMAT 2026 | Graduate Management Admission Council | 2 November to 20 December 2026 | 120 min, 108 questions | None |
| MAT | All India Management Association | Multiple cycles a year | As per the AIMA bulletin | As per the AIMA bulletin |

Three differences are worth planning around. XAT includes a decision making section that no other exam has, and it penalises leaving more than eight questions unattempted, which is a rule unique to it. NMAT allows multiple attempts within its window and lets you choose your section order, which suits candidates who perform better with a familiar sequence. SNAP is much shorter at 60 minutes, so it rewards speed over stamina.

Because the dates are spread from late November to early January, sitting three or four of these costs mainly registration fees and a few weekends, and it widens the set of institutes available to you considerably. Our pages on [XAT 2027](/entrance-exams/xat-2027), [SNAP 2026](/entrance-exams/snap-2026) and [NMAT 2026](/entrance-exams/nmat-2026) cover each in detail.

## What happens after the CAT result

A percentile is the beginning of the admission process rather than the end of it, and candidates focused entirely on the exam are often unprepared for what follows.

Institutes release shortlists in January and February based on the CAT percentile combined with their own weightage formula, which typically includes Class 10 and Class 12 marks, graduation performance, work experience and diversity factors. Two candidates with the same percentile can receive very different call sets because of academic record alone.

Shortlisted candidates attend a selection round, usually some combination of a Written Ability Test, a group discussion or group exercise, and a personal interview. The final offer is computed from a formula that gives the CAT percentile a defined weight alongside these components, and at several institutes the exam accounts for less than half of the final score.

This has a practical consequence for anyone reading this in August. Preparation for the interview stage, which means being able to discuss your own academic background, work, and reasons for an MBA coherently, is worth starting well before the result rather than in the fortnight after it.

## Mistakes that cost candidates marks

Ignoring the sectional time limit in practice. Candidates who take mocks without enforcing the 40-minute lock arrive on exam day with time-allocation habits that the software will not permit.

Leaving TITA questions blank. There are 23 of them carrying no penalty, and every blank one is a guaranteed zero in place of a free attempt.

Starting too many DILR sets. Completing two sets fully scores better than beginning four and finishing none, and set selection in the opening minutes is the highest-value decision in the section.

Abandoning a weak section entirely. Sectional percentiles are computed separately and most institutes enforce sectional cutoffs, so a zero-effort section can end an application that a strong overall percentile would otherwise carry.

Preparing VARC from grammar and vocabulary material. Recent papers test reading comprehension rather than rules, so the useful preparation is sustained reading of dense argumentative prose.

Taking mocks without analysing them. The analysis is where the improvement happens, and it deserves at least as much time as the attempt.

## How to apply

Applications are filed only on iimcat.ac.in.

1. Register with a valid email address and mobile number, both of which are used for all communication including the admit card.
2. Complete the application with academic details exactly as on your certificates, since percentages entered here feed institute shortlisting.
3. Select your programme preferences across the participating IIMs.
4. Choose your preferred test cities in order, since allotment follows that order and your travel plans depend on it.
5. Upload photograph and signature in the specified format and size.
6. Pay the fee of Rs 2,700, or Rs 1,350 for SC, ST and PwD candidates.
7. Submit and save the application, then download the admit card between 4 and 29 November 2026.

## Documents you will need

1. Class 10 and Class 12 mark sheets and certificates.
2. Graduation mark sheets and degree certificate, or a bonafide certificate if you are in the final year.
3. Category certificate in the prescribed central government format for NC-OBC, SC, ST and EWS claims, issued within the validity period stated in the bulletin.
4. PwD certificate where applicable.
5. Work experience certificates where you intend to claim experience at the interview stage.
6. Photograph, signature and a photo identity document matching the application.

## RRB Group D 2026: the CBT is over and the answer key is out

RRB Group D 2026, advertised as CEN 09/2025, fills 22,195 Level 1 posts in Indian Railways. Its Computer Based Test ran from 3 to 25 August 2026 across 16 days, in three shifts a day at more than 200 centres, and the Railway Recruitment Boards published the provisional answer key on 7 September 2026. The objection window that followed it has closed.

What is left is the result, which the RRBs have not dated. Normalisation can only be applied once every shift is accounted for, so the result is expected towards the end of October 2026. The admit card was released from 31 July 2026 and the city intimation slip from 24 July 2026, both on rrbapply.gov.in and the regional RRB websites.

This is one of the largest recruitment exercises anywhere. Reported applicant figures vary widely across sources, from around 58 lakh to close to a crore, and the exact number is not something any secondary site can confirm. Either way, 22,195 posts against a field that size means the Computer Based Test is decided on a handful of marks, and the negative marking on this paper is the reason many candidates lose them.

## The CBT schedule as it ran

The Railway Recruitment Board revised this schedule once during the cycle. These are the days the exam was held on.

| Week | Dates in August 2026 |
|---|---|
| First | 3, 4, 5, 6 |
| Second | 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14 |
| Third | 17, 18, 19, 20, 21 |
| Fourth | 25 |

Sixteen days, three shifts each, which means a large number of distinct question papers. Because of that, RRB applies normalisation across shifts, so your final score is adjusted for the relative difficulty of the paper you sat rather than taken as a raw total. A candidate who gets a harder shift is not penalised for it, and equally a raw score from an easier shift does not carry the advantage it appears to.

## Why you are seeing two sets of contradictory dates

Search for RRB Group D right now and you will find pages announcing that the CBT is starting alongside pages announcing that PET dates are out and results have been declared. Both are accurate. They describe different recruitment cycles.

| Cycle | Stage in September 2026 |
|---|---|
| CEN 08/2024 | Result declared, at the Physical Efficiency Test and later stages |
| CEN 09/2025 | CBT completed 25 August 2026, answer key out, result awaited |

If you applied in the current round, yours is CEN 09/2025 and the result is your live stage. The PET notices circulating now belong to the earlier cycle and do not apply to you. Check the CEN number on your admit card if you are unsure, because acting on the wrong cycle's notice is the most common avoidable error in railway recruitment.

## Exam day: what to carry and what to expect

Take the printed admit card and the original photo identity document whose details you entered in your application. RRB is strict on the identity document matching the application, and a mismatch is grounds for being turned away.

Reach the centre by the reporting time on the admit card, not the exam start time. Gates close well before the paper begins, and RRB does not admit latecomers. Biometric verification and document checks take time, which is why the reporting window opens so far ahead.

Electronic items are prohibited: mobile phones, smart watches, calculators, Bluetooth devices and any storage media. So are bags, written material and, at most centres, metallic items and jewellery. Centres do not reliably provide storage, so carry as little as possible.

The paper is 90 minutes, extended to 120 minutes for candidates with a disability who have been granted a scribe or compensatory time.

## Exam pattern

The CBT is a single objective paper of 100 questions.

| Section | Questions | Marks |
|---|---|---|
| General Intelligence and Reasoning | 30 | 30 |
| Mathematics | 25 | 25 |
| General Science | 25 | 25 |
| General Awareness and Current Affairs | 20 | 20 |
| Total | 100 | 100 |

Duration is 90 minutes. Each correct answer carries 1 mark, and one third of a mark is deducted for each wrong answer.

That negative marking deserves attention, because several other recruitments carry none and the habits do not transfer. Work the arithmetic. A correct answer gains 1, a wrong one costs 0.33. Guessing blindly among four options gives you one correct and three wrong on average, so 1 minus 0.99, which is essentially break-even with added variance and no real gain. Eliminate one option and the odds tilt in your favour. Eliminate two and answering is clearly correct.

The practical rule: answer everything you know or can narrow to two options, and leave alone the questions where you have no basis at all. Candidates who carry an attempt-everything habit from exams like UP Police or Bihar Police, where there is no penalty, hand back marks here.

## Qualifying marks

Clearing the paper requires a minimum percentage that varies by category, commonly applied as 40 per cent for unreserved and EWS candidates, 30 per cent for OBC and SC, and 25 per cent for ST, with relaxation for candidates with disabilities where there is a shortfall.

Meeting that minimum is not selection. It makes you eligible to be ranked, and the actual shortlisting for the PET is done on normalised merit against the vacancy position in your region, which sits far above the qualifying floor.

## Syllabus

The paper is pitched at Class 10 level and rewards coverage more than depth.

Reasoning carries the most questions at 30 and covers analogies, series completion, coding and decoding, mathematical operations, relationships, syllogism, Venn diagrams, data interpretation, statement and conclusion, directions and analytical reasoning. It is the most trainable section, since the question types repeat and practice converts directly into speed.

Mathematics covers number systems, decimals and fractions, LCM and HCF, ratio and proportion, percentages, mensuration, time and work, time and distance, simple and compound interest, profit and loss, algebra, geometry and trigonometry basics, elementary statistics, and age and calendar problems.

General Science covers physics, chemistry and life sciences at Class 10 level. Physics and chemistry tend to carry more weight than biology in recent papers.

General Awareness and Current Affairs covers science and technology, sports, culture, personalities, economics, politics and general current affairs, with a bias towards the last year and towards railway-related developments.

## What the Level 1 posts actually are

Level 1 covers six categories of post, and they are different jobs despite sharing an entry route.

Pointsman operates points and signals at stations and yards, a safety-critical outdoor role often on night shifts. Track Maintainer Grade IV maintains the permanent way, which is physically demanding outdoor work on the track itself. Assistant posts in the Loco Shed, in Operations, and in TL and AC support maintenance and operations in depots and on trains. The remaining assistant categories cover workshop and departmental support roles.

Post preference is exercised during the application and allocation follows merit, region and vacancy position. Almost all of these involve shift work, outdoor conditions and a physical component, which is why the recruitment carries a Physical Efficiency Test at all.

## Physical Efficiency Test

The PET is pass or fail. It adds no marks to your merit position, and failing it removes you regardless of your CBT score.

| Candidates | Lifting and carrying | Running |
|---|---|---|
| Male | 35 kg carried over 100 metres in under 2 minutes, in one go without setting it down | 1000 metres in 4 minutes 15 seconds |
| Female | 20 kg carried over 100 metres in under 2 minutes, in one go without setting it down | 1000 metres in 5 minutes 40 seconds |

The lifting event is the one candidates underestimate, and the condition attached to it is what makes it hard: the weight has to be carried the full 100 metres in a single attempt without being put down. That is a grip strength and carrying endurance problem more than a maximal strength one, and it is not something general gym work prepares you for specifically. Loaded carries, farmer's walks and grip work are the training that transfers.

The running standard is more forgiving. 1000 metres in 4 minutes 15 seconds for men works out to about 4 minutes 15 seconds per kilometre, which is demanding but well short of the 800 metre standards in state police recruitment.

Both events are attempted in sequence and both must be cleared.

## Selection process

| Stage | Role |
|---|---|
| Computer Based Test | Decides merit, after normalisation across shifts |
| Physical Efficiency Test | Qualifying only |
| Document Verification | Eligibility check |
| Medical Examination | Fitness against the medical standard for the post |

The medical standard varies by post, and it is stricter than candidates expect for safety-related categories. Vision requirements for Pointsman and other safety posts in particular rule out candidates who would pass the standard for a clerical role, so check the medical classification for the posts you have preferenced.

## Salary of an RRB Group D employee

Level 1 of the 7th Pay Commission matrix carries a basic pay of Rs 18,000 a month, with an annual increment of about Rs 500 at the entry stage.

On top of basic pay come dearness allowance at the prevailing rate, house rent allowance at 8, 16 or 24 per cent of basic depending on the classification of your posting city, transport allowance, and railway-specific allowances including running or shift allowances where the post attracts them. Taking those together, in-hand pay at entry commonly works out in the region of Rs 22,500 to Rs 25,380 a month depending on posting and the current DA rate.

The non-cash side matters in railway service more than in most government jobs. Railway quarters where available, the free or concessional pass entitlement for the employee and family, railway medical facilities through railway hospitals, and pension benefits under the applicable rules all carry real value that the headline figure understates.

## Career progression

Level 1 is the entry rung and progression runs through departmental channels.

| Stage | Route |
|---|---|
| Level 1 entry post | Direct recruitment |
| Level 2 and 3 | Departmental promotion and departmental examinations |
| Higher technical and supervisory grades | Selection posts through departmental examination |

Indian Railways runs an internal promotion system with a defined quota of higher posts filled from serving employees through the General Departmental Competitive Examination and other departmental routes. A Level 1 entrant who prepares for those examinations can move up materially over a career, and many technical supervisors began at this level.

## How to use the remaining exam days

Because the CBT runs to 25 August, a large share of candidates still have days or weeks before they sit it, and that time is better spent on the paper's specific demands than on fresh study.

Reasoning is where the marginal marks are. It carries the most questions at 30, the question types repeat across cycles, and speed on them is a trained skill rather than a knowledge one. Working timed sets of past reasoning questions is the highest-return use of a remaining week.

Practise at the real pace. 100 questions in 90 minutes gives you 54 seconds per question, and the paper is not designed for careful deliberation on every item. Candidates lose more to poor time allocation, spending four minutes on a hard maths question, than to gaps in knowledge.

Rehearse the marking decision. Take a full mock, mark each answer as confident, narrowed to two, or pure guess, then score it both ways: once counting your guesses and once leaving them blank. Doing that twice tells you your own accuracy rate on narrowed questions, which is a better guide to exam-day behaviour than any general rule about negative marking.

Revise general science and current affairs last, since those are recall-heavy and benefit from being fresh.

## Eligibility

On age, the band for the cycle is set in the CEN, commonly 18 to 36 years for Level 1 posts with relaxation of 3 years for OBC, 5 years for SC and ST, and further relaxation for ex-servicemen and other specified categories.

On education, the requirement is Class 10 pass, or an ITI certificate from an institution recognised by NCVT or SCVT, or an equivalent National Apprenticeship Certificate. A Class 10 pass alone is sufficient for most Level 1 posts.

On medical fitness, each post carries a medical classification and candidates must meet the standard for the post allotted, with vision requirements being the most common ground for rejection in safety categories.

## What happens after the CBT

The last shift was held on 25 August 2026 and the provisional answer key came out on 7 September 2026, with objections closing after it. The result follows once normalisation is applied across every shift, which the RRBs have not dated and which past cycles put at roughly two months after the final shift.

Shortlisted candidates are called for the PET, then document verification, then the medical. Use the intervening period rather than waiting on the result. The lifting standard in particular takes weeks of specific training to build, and candidates who begin only after the shortlist is published arrive underprepared for an event that is pass or fail.

Keep your documents ready in the meantime: Class 10 certificate, ITI or NAC certificate where relied on, category certificate in the central government format with a current non-creamy layer certificate for OBC candidates, and the identity documents matching your application.

## Frequently asked questions

**When is the RRB Group D 2026 exam?**
The Computer Based Test for CEN 09/2025 runs across 16 days in August 2026: the 3rd, 4th, 5th, 6th, 9th, 10th, 11th, 12th, 13th, 14th, 17th, 18th, 19th, 20th, 21st and 25th, in three shifts a day at more than 200 centres. The schedule was revised, so rely on the date printed on your admit card rather than an earlier notice.

**How do I download the RRB Group D admit card 2026?**
Admit cards were released from 31 July 2026 on rrbapply.gov.in and the regional Railway Recruitment Board websites, four days before the first exam date. The city intimation slip, which tells you your exam city ahead of the admit card, was released from 24 July 2026. Log in with your registration number and date of birth.

**Is there negative marking in RRB Group D?**
Yes. One third of a mark is deducted for each wrong answer, against 1 mark for a correct one. Blind guessing among four options is roughly break-even and adds variance, so answer where you know the answer or can narrow it to two options, and leave the rest. RRB Group D 2026, advertised as CEN 09/2025, fills 22,195 Level 1 posts in Indian Railways. Its Computer Based Test ran from 3 to 25 August 2026 across 16 days, in three shifts a day at more than 200 centres, and the Railway Recruitment Boards published the provisional answer key on 7 September 2026. The objection window that followed it has closed.

What is left is the result, which the RRBs have not dated. Normalisation can only be applied once every shift is accounted for, so the result is expected towards the end of October 2026 rather than in September. The admit card was released from 31 July 2026 and the city intimation slip from 24 July 2026, both on rrbapply.gov.in and the regional RRB websites.

This is one of the largest recruitment exercises anywhere. Reported applicant figures vary widely across sources, from around 58 lakh to close to a crore, and the exact number is not something any secondary site can confirm. Either way, 22,195 posts against a field that size means the Computer Based Test is decided on a handful of marks, and the negative marking on this paper is the reason many candidates lose them.

## The CBT schedule as it ran

The Railway Recruitment Board revised this schedule once during the cycle. These are the days the exam was held on.

| Week | Dates in August 2026 |
|---|---|
| First | 3, 4, 5, 6 |
| Second | 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14 |
| Third | 17, 18, 19, 20, 21 |
| Fourth | 25 |

Sixteen days, three shifts each, which means a large number of distinct question papers. Because of that, RRB applies normalisation across shifts, so your final score is adjusted for the relative difficulty of the paper you sat rather than taken as a raw total. A candidate who gets a harder shift is not penalised for it, and equally a raw score from an easier shift does not carry the advantage it appears to.

## Why you are seeing two sets of contradictory dates

Search for RRB Group D right now and you will find pages announcing that the CBT is starting alongside pages announcing that PET dates are out and results have been declared. Both are accurate. They describe different recruitment cycles.

| Cycle | Stage in September 2026 |
|---|---|
| CEN 08/2024 | Result declared, at the Physical Efficiency Test and later stages |
| CEN 09/2025 | CBT completed 25 August 2026, answer key out, result awaited |

If you applied in the current round, yours is CEN 09/2025 and the result is your live stage. The PET notices circulating now belong to the earlier cycle and do not apply to you. Check the CEN number on your admit card if you are unsure, because acting on the wrong cycle's notice is the most common avoidable error in railway recruitment.

## Exam day: what to carry and what to expect

Take the printed admit card and the original photo identity document whose details you entered in your application. RRB is strict on the identity document matching the application, and a mismatch is grounds for being turned away.

Reach the centre by the reporting time on the admit card, not the exam start time. Gates close well before the paper begins, and RRB does not admit latecomers. Biometric verification and document checks take time, which is why the reporting window opens so far ahead.

Electronic items are prohibited: mobile phones, smart watches, calculators, Bluetooth devices and any storage media. So are bags, written material and, at most centres, metallic items and jewellery. Centres do not reliably provide storage, so carry as little as possible.

The paper is 90 minutes, extended to 120 minutes for candidates with a disability who have been granted a scribe or compensatory time.

## Exam pattern

The CBT is a single objective paper of 100 questions.

| Section | Questions | Marks |
|---|---|---|
| General Intelligence and Reasoning | 30 | 30 |
| Mathematics | 25 | 25 |
| General Science | 25 | 25 |
| General Awareness and Current Affairs | 20 | 20 |
| Total | 100 | 100 |

Duration is 90 minutes. Each correct answer carries 1 mark, and one third of a mark is deducted for each wrong answer.

That negative marking deserves attention, because several other recruitments carry none and the habits do not transfer. Work the arithmetic. A correct answer gains 1, a wrong one costs 0.33. Guessing blindly among four options gives you one correct and three wrong on average, so 1 minus 0.99, which is essentially break-even with added variance and no real gain. Eliminate one option and the odds tilt in your favour. Eliminate two and answering is clearly correct.

The practical rule: answer everything you know or can narrow to two options, and leave alone the questions where you have no basis at all. Candidates who carry an attempt-everything habit from exams like UP Police or Bihar Police, where there is no penalty, hand back marks here.

## Qualifying marks

Clearing the paper requires a minimum percentage that varies by category, commonly applied as 40 per cent for unreserved and EWS candidates, 30 per cent for OBC and SC, and 25 per cent for ST, with relaxation for candidates with disabilities where there is a shortfall.

Meeting that minimum is not selection. It makes you eligible to be ranked, and the actual shortlisting for the PET is done on normalised merit against the vacancy position in your region, which sits far above the qualifying floor.

## Syllabus

The paper is pitched at Class 10 level and rewards coverage more than depth.

Reasoning carries the most questions at 30 and covers analogies, series completion, coding and decoding, mathematical operations, relationships, syllogism, Venn diagrams, data interpretation, statement and conclusion, directions and analytical reasoning. It is the most trainable section, since the question types repeat and practice converts directly into speed.

Mathematics covers number systems, decimals and fractions, LCM and HCF, ratio and proportion, percentages, mensuration, time and work, time and distance, simple and compound interest, profit and loss, algebra, geometry and trigonometry basics, elementary statistics, and age and calendar problems.

General Science covers physics, chemistry and life sciences at Class 10 level. Physics and chemistry tend to carry more weight than biology in recent papers.

General Awareness and Current Affairs covers science and technology, sports, culture, personalities, economics, politics and general current affairs, with a bias towards the last year and towards railway-related developments.

## What the Level 1 posts actually are

Level 1 covers six categories of post, and they are different jobs despite sharing an entry route.

Pointsman operates points and signals at stations and yards, a safety-critical outdoor role often on night shifts. Track Maintainer Grade IV maintains the permanent way, which is physically demanding outdoor work on the track itself. Assistant posts in the Loco Shed, in Operations, and in TL and AC support maintenance and operations in depots and on trains. The remaining assistant categories cover workshop and departmental support roles.

Post preference is exercised during the application and allocation follows merit, region and vacancy position. Almost all of these involve shift work, outdoor conditions and a physical component, which is why the recruitment carries a Physical Efficiency Test at all.

## Physical Efficiency Test

The PET is pass or fail. It adds no marks to your merit position, and failing it removes you regardless of your CBT score.

| Candidates | Lifting and carrying | Running |
|---|---|---|
| Male | 35 kg carried over 100 metres in under 2 minutes, in one go without setting it down | 1000 metres in 4 minutes 15 seconds |
| Female | 20 kg carried over 100 metres in under 2 minutes, in one go without setting it down | 1000 metres in 5 minutes 40 seconds |

The lifting event is the one candidates underestimate, and the condition attached to it is what makes it hard: the weight has to be carried the full 100 metres in a single attempt without being put down. That is a grip strength and carrying endurance problem more than a maximal strength one, and it is not something general gym work prepares you for specifically. Loaded carries, farmer's walks and grip work are the training that transfers.

The running standard is more forgiving. 1000 metres in 4 minutes 15 seconds for men works out to about 4 minutes 15 seconds per kilometre, which is demanding but well short of the 800 metre standards in state police recruitment.

Both events are attempted in sequence and both must be cleared.

| Stage | Role |
|---|---|
| Computer Based Test | Decides merit, after normalisation across shifts |
| Physical Efficiency Test | Qualifying only |
| Document Verification | Eligibility check |
| Medical Examination | Fitness against the medical standard for the post |

The medical standard varies by post, and it is stricter than candidates expect for safety-related categories. Vision requirements for Pointsman and other safety posts in particular rule out candidates who would pass the standard for a clerical role, so check the medical classification for the posts you have preferenced.

Level 1 of the 7th Pay Commission matrix carries a basic pay of Rs 18,000 a month, with an annual increment of about Rs 500 at the entry stage.

Taking those together, in-hand pay at entry commonly works out in the region of Rs 22,500 to Rs 25,380 a month depending on posting and the current DA rate.

The non-cash side matters in railway service more than in most government jobs. Railway quarters where available, the free or concessional pass entitlement for the employee and family, railway medical facilities through railway hospitals, and pension benefits under the applicable rules all carry real value that the headline figure understates.

## Career progression

Level 1 is the entry rung and progression runs through departmental channels.

| Stage | Route |
|---|---|
| Level 1 entry post | Direct recruitment |
| Level 2 and 3 | Departmental promotion and departmental examinations |
| Higher technical and supervisory grades | Selection posts through departmental examination |

Indian Railways runs an internal promotion system with a defined quota of higher posts filled from serving employees through the General Departmental Competitive Examination and other departmental routes. A Level 1 entrant who prepares for those examinations can move up materially over a career, and many technical supervisors began at this level.

## How to use the remaining exam days

Because the CBT runs to 25 August, a large share of candidates still have days or weeks before they sit it, and that time is better spent on the paper's specific demands than on fresh study.

Reasoning is where the marginal marks are. It carries the most questions at 30, the question types repeat across cycles, and speed on them is a trained skill rather than a knowledge one. Working timed sets of past reasoning questions is the highest-return use of a remaining week.

Practise at the real pace. 100 questions in 90 minutes gives you 54 seconds per question, and the paper is not designed for careful deliberation on every item. Candidates lose more to poor time allocation, spending four minutes on a hard maths question, than to gaps in knowledge.

Rehearse the marking decision. Take a full mock, mark each answer as confident, narrowed to two, or pure guess, then score it both ways: once counting your guesses and once leaving them blank. Doing that twice tells you your own accuracy rate on narrowed questions, which is a better guide to exam-day behaviour than any general rule about negative marking.

Revise general science and current affairs last, since those are recall-heavy and benefit from being fresh.

On age, the band for the cycle is set in the CEN, commonly 18 to 36 years for Level 1 posts with relaxation of 3 years for OBC, 5 years for SC and ST, and further relaxation for ex-servicemen and other specified categories.

On medical fitness, each post carries a medical classification and candidates must meet the standard for the post allotted, with vision requirements being the most common ground for rejection in safety categories.

The last shift was held on 25 August 2026 and the provisional answer key came out on 7 September 2026, with objections closing after it. The result follows once normalisation is applied across every shift, which the RRBs have not dated and which past cycles put at roughly two months after the final shift.

Shortlisted candidates are called for the PET, then document verification, then the medical. Use the intervening period rather than waiting on the result. The lifting standard in particular takes weeks of specific training to build, and candidates who begin only after the shortlist is published arrive underprepared for an event that is pass or fail.
